rows.translation: 安娜莉没有讲述什么英勇事迹，而是调整了一下握拐杖的姿势，说道：“如果你不介意，我不太想谈。私下里我已经想得够多了，谢谢。”
rows.raw: "\n\nInstead of opening up about exploits, Anarrie adjusts her grip on her cane and says, “I’d rather not, if it’s all the same to you. I think about it enough on my own time, thanks.”"

rows.original: She taps her cane against her left leg, which answers with a dull metallic thump! There’s something very final about the gesture that does not invite further inquiry.
rows.translation: 她用拐杖敲了敲左腿，裤子下面传来沉闷的金属砰！声。这个动作透着不容置疑的终结意味，显然不欢迎你继续追问。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe taps her cane against her left leg, which answers with a dull metallic thump! There’s something very final about the gesture that does not invite further inquiry."

rows.original: Fed. Army
rows.translation: 联邦军队
rows.raw: "Fed. Army"

rows.original: Federation Army
rows.translation: 联邦军队
rows.raw: "Federation Army"

rows.original: Ask Anarrie about her experience in the Federation military. Red myr do love their war stories...
rows.translation: 向安娜莉询问她在联邦军队的经历。红米尔确实很喜欢讲战争故事...
rows.raw: "Ask Anarrie about her experience in the Federation military. Red myr do love their war stories..."

rows.original: Her Shop
rows.translation: 她的商店
rows.raw: "Her Shop"

rows.original: “How’d you end up all the way out here running a shop?” you ask, glancing around the cozy little storefront.
rows.translation: “你怎么会大老远跑到这里开店？”你环顾温馨的小店，问道。
rows.raw: "“How’d you end up all the way out here running a shop?” you ask, glancing around the cozy little storefront."

rows.original: “You’re a long way from home, after all.”
rows.translation: “毕竟这里离你的家乡很远。”
rows.raw: " “You’re a long way from home, after all.”"

rows.original: The red myr woman laughs, leaning back in her chair. “It’s a funny story, actually. Right after I was discharged, a lot of us wounded veterans were offered free airlifts to the region by your Confederacy’s medical company. Xenogen, I think? They were offering those of us who needed it these cybernetic replacements and other wound treatment. Your medical technology is many years more advanced than ours, I have to admit. The people who operated on us worked miracles. When I woke up after they’d finished operating on me, though, almost all of the women I’d come with had already returned home, and there were no more direct transports back to the heartland. Apparently I had some sort of allergic reaction to the anesthetic they gave me, and stayed in a coma for an extra week.”
rows.translation: 红米尔女人笑了起来，靠回椅背。“其实是个挺有趣的故事。我刚退伍时，你们联盟的一家医疗公司为许多伤残老兵提供免费空运。好像叫异源生物科技？他们给有需要的人提供这些义体替代品和其他创伤治疗。我得承认，你们的医疗技术比我们先进很多年。给我们做手术的人简直创造了奇迹。不过，等我在手术结束后醒来时，和我一起来的女人几乎都已经回家了，也没有直达内地的交通工具。据说我对他们使用的麻醉剂产生了某种过敏反应，多昏迷了整整一周。”
rows.raw: "\n\nThe red myr woman laughs, leaning back in her chair. “It’s a funny story, actually. Right after I was discharged, a lot of us wounded veterans were offered free airlifts to the region by your Confederacy’s medical company. Xenogen, I think? They were offering those of us who needed it these cybernetic replacements and other wound treatment. Your medical technology is many years more advanced than ours, I have to admit. The people who operated on us worked miracles. When I woke up after they’d finished operating on me, though, almost all of the women I’d come with had already returned home, and there were no more direct transports back to the heartland. Apparently I had some sort of allergic reaction to the anesthetic they gave me, and stayed in a coma for an extra week.”"

rows.original: She gives a wry chuckle and rubs at her left knee, which makes a metallic clicking sound under her pants. “When the doctor, some sort of half-horse woman, finally released me, I decided to take advantage of the cease fire that had been declared - and my newfound mobility - to walk for a while. I ended up in Kressia pretty much by accident, just wandering through the trenches. The old battlefields have a weird beauty to them, silent and oppressive. If you ever have the chance to walk through them, do it.”
rows.translation: 她苦笑一声，揉了揉左膝，裤子下面随即响起金属咔嗒声。“医生终于准许我出院时——她好像是个半马女人——我决定利用已经宣布的停火，还有我重新获得的行动能力，四处走走。我几乎是偶然间来到克雷西亚的，只是漫无目的地穿过战壕。旧战场有一种诡异的美，寂静又压抑。要是你有机会走一遍，千万别错过。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe gives a wry chuckle and rubs at her left knee, which makes a metallic clicking sound under her pants. “When the doctor, some sort of half-horse woman, finally released me, I decided to take advantage of the cease fire that had been declared - and my newfound mobility - to walk for a while. I ended up in Kressia pretty much by accident, just wandering through the trenches. The old battlefields have a weird beauty to them, silent and oppressive. If you ever have the chance to walk through them, do it.”"

rows.original: “Old battlefields are beautiful? Now that’s morbid,” Shiare says with what must be the myr equivalent of rolling her eyes.
rows.translation: “旧战场很美？这也太阴森了，”希娅蕾说道，做出一个大概相当于米尔人翻白眼的表情。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Old battlefields are beautiful? Now that’s morbid,” Shiare says with what must be the myr equivalent of rolling her eyes."

rows.original: Anarrie just scowls. “ANYway, I wandered into Kressia, just in time to see the first waves of you... what do you call yourselves - planet-rushers? - coming in from the airfield. They were so completely in awe of the city: ‘an underground civilization, what will they think of next?’ Ha. None of them had done cave exploration before, and here I was at the nexus of the airfield, the trenches, and the biggest access to the deep caves there is for miles around. There were plenty of empty storefronts around, and I knew a little about being a merchant, so... I wrote Shiare and told her to pack her bags. Money to be made.”
rows.translation: 安娜莉只是皱起眉头。“总、之，我走进克雷西亚时，正好看到第一批你们这些...你们怎么称呼自己来着——行星淘金者？——从机场涌来。他们对这座城市惊叹不已：‘地下文明，他们下次还能想出什么？’哈。他们谁都没进行过洞穴探险，而我正好身处机场、战壕和方圆数英里内最大深层洞穴入口的交汇处。附近有不少空店面，我也懂一点经商，所以...我写信让希娅蕾收拾行李。这里有钱可赚。”
rows.raw: "\n\nAnarrie just scowls. “ANYway, I wandered into Kressia, just in time to see the first waves of you... what do you call yourselves - planet-rushers? - coming in from the airfield. They were so completely in awe of the city: ‘an underground civilization, what will they think of next?’ Ha. None of them had done cave exploration before, and here I was at the nexus of the airfield, the trenches, and the biggest access to the deep caves there is for miles around. There were plenty of empty storefronts around, and I knew a little about being a merchant, so... I wrote Shiare and told her to pack her bags. Money to be made.”"

rows.original: “What she didn’t say is that this place was going to be a fixer-upper,” Shiare adds, waving one of her four arms around the shop. “A bomb went off just down the street, so we didn’t have any windows, the walls were banged up...”
rows.translation: “她没说的是，这地方当时得彻底翻修，”希娅蕾补充道，用四条手臂中的一条指了指店里。“街边不远处炸过一枚炸弹，所以窗户全没了，墙也被炸得坑坑洼洼...”
rows.raw: "\n\n“What she didn’t say is that this place was going to be a fixer-upper,” Shiare adds, waving one of her four arms around the shop. “A bomb went off just down the street, so we didn’t have any windows, the walls were banged up...”"

rows.original: “But we made it work,” Anarrie finishes with a smile. “Anybody who’s thinking about going out in No Myr’s Land learns pretty quick to stop in here first. Trust me, you don’t wanna go out there without one of our minesweepers to clear the path, or a good flare gun to light the way.”
rows.translation: “但我们还是把它经营起来了，”安娜莉微笑着结束话题。“任何打算前往无米尔之地的人，很快都会明白必须先来这里。相信我，要是没有我们的扫雷器清出道路，或者一把好用的信号枪照明，你绝对不想去外面。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“But we made it work,” Anarrie finishes with a smile. “Anybody who’s thinking about going out in No Myr’s Land learns pretty quick to stop in here first. Trust me, you don’t wanna go out there without one of our minesweepers to clear the path, or a good flare gun to light the way.”"

rows.original: Her Shop
rows.translation: 她的商店
rows.raw: "Her Shop"

rows.original: Her Shop
rows.translation: 她的商店
rows.raw: "Her Shop"

rows.original: So how did Anarrie end up all the way out in Kressia and running a store?
rows.translation: 安娜莉究竟为何大老远来到克雷西亚，还在这里经营商店？
rows.raw: "So how did Anarrie end up all the way out in Kressia and running a store?"

rows.original: Venom Vials
rows.translation: 毒液瓶
rows.raw: "Venom Vials"

rows.original: “Is that ‘red venom’ what I think it is?” you ask, rapping a knuckle on the glass display case, just over the arrangement of pink-filled vials.
rows.translation: “那种‘红色毒液’就是我想的那个东西吗？”你问道，用指节敲了敲玻璃陈列柜，位置正好在一排装满粉色液体的小瓶上方。
rows.raw: "“Is that ‘red venom’ what I think it is?” you ask, rapping a knuckle on the glass display case, just over the arrangement of pink-filled vials."

rows.original: Anarrie answers with a surprisingly nonchalant nod. “It is. The Republic’s Queens outlaw it in their territory as a dangerous drug, but there’s no proscription against its sale now that Kressia is in Federation territory. It’s hard to regulate something any one of us can spit out, after all. Besides, its sale serves a necessary function here, keeping trench wives from going into withdrawal if their mistresses need to leave them alone for a short time, and making sure any addicts can continue to function without having to rely on another woman constantly.”
rows.translation: 安娜莉出乎意料地漫不经心地点头。“没错。共和国的女王们将它视为危险药物，在领地内明令禁止，但克雷西亚如今属于联邦领土，并没有法律禁止销售。毕竟，我们任何一个人都能吐出这种东西，很难监管。而且，在这里出售它确实有必要：如果女主人必须短暂离开，可以避免战壕妻子出现戒断反应，也能让成瘾者继续正常生活，不必时时依赖另一个女人。”
rows.raw: "\n\nAnarrie answers with a surprisingly nonchalant nod. “It is. The Republic’s Queens outlaw it in their territory as a dangerous drug, but there’s no proscription against its sale now that Kressia is in Federation territory. It’s hard to regulate something any one of us can spit out, after all. Besides, its sale serves a necessary function here, keeping trench wives from going into withdrawal if their mistresses need to leave them alone for a short time, and making sure any addicts can continue to function without having to rely on another woman constantly.”"

rows.original: With a conspiratorial look around, she bids you to lean down a little closer. When you do, she continues: <i>“Some might think it’s very... let’s say ‘erotic’... to become addicted to a lover’s vital essence, but let’s be honest: it’s not very practical to be constantly reliant on anybody, even your wife.
rows.translation: 她神秘兮兮地四下张望，示意你再靠近一点。你照做后，她继续说道：<i>“有些人可能觉得，对爱人的生命精华上瘾非常...姑且说‘色情’吧...但说实话：时时依赖任何人都很不实际，哪怕那个人是你的妻子。
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a conspiratorial look around, she bids you to lean down a little closer. When you do, she continues: <i>“Some might think it’s very... let’s say ‘erotic’... to become addicted to a lover’s vital essence, but let’s be honest: it’s not very practical to be constantly reliant on anybody, even your wife."

rows.original: With a hint of pride, she adds, <i>“
rows.translation: 她略带自豪地补充道，<i>“
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a hint of pride, she adds, <i>“"

rows.original: If there’s anything I try and foster here in my shop, it’s self-reliance. Independence.”
rows.translation: 如果说我想在这家店里培养什么，那就是自力更生。独立。”
rows.raw: "If there’s anything I try and foster here in my shop, it’s self-reliance. Independence.”"

rows.original: From the other counter, her lover chuckles and says, “Come on, Ana, you’d be helpless without me!”
rows.translation: 另一边的柜台传来她爱人的轻笑：“得了吧，安娜，没有我你什么都做不了！”
rows.raw: "\n\nFrom the other counter, her lover chuckles and says, “Come on, Ana, you’d be helpless without me!”"

rows.original: “Only emotionally, I’ll have you know,” the red answers with indignation. “Besides, if I wasn’t around, you’d never be able to reach anything on the top shelves.”
rows.translation: “只是在感情上，我可得说明白，”红米尔愤愤不平地回答。“再说，要是没有我，你根本够不着顶层架子上的任何东西。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Only emotionally, I’ll have you know,” the red answers with indignation. “Besides, if I wasn’t around, you’d never be able to reach anything on the top shelves.”"

rows.original: Shiare bursts out laughing. “So you’re a glorified stepladder, is that it?”
rows.translation: 希娅蕾放声大笑。“所以你就是个豪华版的活梯子，对吧？”
rows.raw: "\n\nShiare bursts out laughing. “So you’re a glorified stepladder, is that it?”"

rows.original: “Dammit,” Anarrie huffs, crossing her arms. Turning back to you, she asks “Any more questions?”
rows.translation: “该死，”安娜莉抱起双臂，气呼呼地说道。她重新转向你，问道：“还有什么问题吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Dammit,” Anarrie huffs, crossing her arms. Turning back to you, she asks “Any more questions?”"

rows.original: You have to ask: where does she get all that venom?
rows.translation: 你不得不问：她哪来那么多毒液？
rows.raw: "\n\nYou have to ask: where does she get all that venom?"

rows.original: “Let’s just say it’s all made made in-house,” Annarie says, giving you a coy look. “I mix mine with just a touch of soda water and honey to make it frothier and sweeter. It’s been pretty popular since we opened, more so than I would have thought. Especially with you star-walkers. Definitely our most popular item with the aliens that come through. Couldn’t tell you why.”
rows.translation: “就当它全是我们自家生产的吧，”安娜莉含蓄地看了你一眼，说道。“我会往自己的毒液里加一点苏打水和蜂蜜，让它泡沫更多、味道更甜。开业以来一直很受欢迎，比我原先预想的还要受欢迎。尤其是在你们这些星行者当中。绝对是最受过往外星人欢迎的商品。至于为什么，我可说不准。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Let’s just say it’s all made made in-house,” Annarie says, giving you a coy look. “I mix mine with just a touch of soda water and honey to make it frothier and sweeter. It’s been pretty popular since we opened, more so than I would have thought. Especially with you star-walkers. Definitely our most popular item with the aliens that come through. Couldn’t tell you why.”"

rows.raw: "No Venom"

rows.original: You’d rather not have your body flooded with myr venom.
rows.translation: 你不想让身体充满米尔毒液。
rows.raw: "You’d rather not have your body flooded with myr venom."

rows.original: Talk
rows.translation: 交谈
rows.raw: "Talk"

rows.original: No Myr’s Land
rows.translation: 无米尔之地
rows.raw: "No Myr’s Land"

rows.original: “Tell me a little about No Myr’s Land,” you prompt. “That’s why they’ve got you out here, right?”
rows.translation: “跟我说说无米尔之地吧，”你开口道。“他们把你派来这里就是为此，对吗？”
rows.raw: "“Tell me a little about No Myr’s Land,” you prompt. “That’s why they’ve got you out here, right?”"

rows.original: “To keep you off-worlders from blundering out there blindly, anyway,” she answers, adding with a mischievous wink: “Apparently it’s bad PR if too many of you step on landmines or something.”
rows.translation: “至少是为了防止你们这些外星人一无所知地闯进去，”她回答道，又顽皮地眨眨眼补充：“显然，要是你们踩地雷的人太多，公关形象会很难看之类的。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“To keep you off-worlders from blundering out there blindly, anyway,” she answers, adding with a mischievous wink: “Apparently it’s bad PR if too many of you step on landmines or something.”"

rows.original: You blink. “Landmines?”
rows.translation: 你眨眨眼。“地雷？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou blink. “Landmines?”"

rows.original: “I’ve noticed a few already,” you grumble.
rows.translation: “我已经发现了几个，”你抱怨道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“I’ve noticed a few already,” you grumble."

rows.original: She nods. “We can’t use artillery down here, Steele. Both sides decided to make up for it by mining the space between the front lines, making it hell for the other to advance. There’s gold myr explosive mines, and our venom vapor ones out there. Either one can ruin your day if you’re not careful. If you haven’t already, go in town and see if you can buy a minesweeper. Cunning little device that picks ‘em up before you step on them. Saved my life more than once.”
rows.translation: 她点点头。“斯蒂尔，我们没法在下面使用火炮。双方于是决定在阵线之间布满地雷作为补偿，让对方难以前进。那里既有金米尔的爆炸地雷，也有我们的毒气地雷。一不小心，任何一种都能毁掉你的一天。要是还没有，就进城看看能不能买到一台扫雷器。那种聪明的小装置会在你踩上去之前发现地雷，已经救过我不止一次。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe nods. “We can’t use artillery down here, Steele. Both sides decided to make up for it by mining the space between the front lines, making it hell for the other to advance. There’s gold myr explosive mines, and our venom vapor ones out there. Either one can ruin your day if you’re not careful. If you haven’t already, go in town and see if you can buy a minesweeper. Cunning little device that picks ‘em up before you step on them. Saved my life more than once.”"

rows.original: “They’re not the worst things you’ll find out there, though,” Lieve adds, inviting you to sit down. You do so as Lieve continues talking. Her voice shifts from the guarded friendliness she normally shows you to a more authoritative pitch, as if she’s talking to one of her subordinates. You imagine she’s given this speech several times before.
rows.translation: “不过它们还不是你会在那里碰到的最糟糕的东西，”莉芙补充道，邀请你坐下。你依言坐好，莉芙继续讲述。她的语气从平时待你时有所戒备的友善，转成了更有权威的腔调，仿佛正与自己的下属讲话。你猜她已经发表过好几次这番演说。
rows.raw: "\n\n“They’re not the worst things you’ll find out there, though,” Lieve adds, inviting you to sit down. You do so as Lieve continues talking. Her voice shifts from the guarded friendliness she normally shows you to a more authoritative pitch, as if she’s talking to one of her subordinates. You imagine she’s given this speech several times before."

rows.original: “Ever since the cease-fire, we’ve gotten plenty of deep dwelling creatures coming back to the surface caves. Most are interested in looting the equipment and supplies left in No Myr’s, others in capturing our patrols or offworlder explorers for... breeding.” Her brow twitches ever so slightly. “The most common threat you’ll face out there are the nyrea. Like us red myr, they’re a warrior race, and damn good at it.”
rows.translation: “自停火以来，许多深居地下的生物都回到了地表洞穴。大部分想洗劫遗留在无米尔之地的装备与补给，其他的则想俘获我们的巡逻队或外星探险者，用来...繁殖。”她的眉头极轻地抽动了一下。“你在那里最常遇到的威胁是尼瑞亚。她们跟我们红米尔一样，是个战士种族，而且非常善战。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Ever since the cease-fire, we’ve gotten plenty of deep dwelling creatures coming back to the surface caves. Most are interested in looting the equipment and supplies left in No Myr’s, others in capturing our patrols or offworlder explorers for... breeding.” Her brow twitches ever so slightly. “The most common threat you’ll face out there are the nyrea. Like us red myr, they’re a warrior race, and damn good at it.”"

rows.original: She gives a wry chuckle at that. <i>“We’ve been fighting the nyrea for years up north. They’re more common there, more organized. Here in the heartlands, though, you’ll mostly be fighting lone huntresses
rows.translation: 她苦笑一声。<i>“我们在北方与尼瑞亚打了很多年。她们在那里更常见，组织也更严密。不过在腹地，你遇到的大多是独自行动的女猎手
rows.raw: "\n\nShe gives a wry chuckle at that. <i>“We’ve been fighting the nyrea for years up north. They’re more common there, more organized. Here in the heartlands, though, you’ll mostly be fighting lone huntresses"

rows.original: keen on stealing your sperm
rows.translation: ，一心想偷走你的精液
rows.raw: " keen on stealing your sperm"

rows.original: that want to borrow your ass or womb to lay their eggs in
rows.translation: ，想借用你的屁股或子宫产卵
rows.raw: " that want to borrow your ass or womb to lay their eggs in"

rows.original: “You’ve fought the nyrea before?” you ask.
rows.translation: “你以前和尼瑞亚交战过？”你问道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“You’ve fought the nyrea before?” you ask."

rows.original: Lieve nods. “Before the war, Federation troops were mainly fighting off nyrea raids. Back in our territory, the nyrea have a few fairly large city-states. One particularly ambitious queen even tried to form a nyrean country, though that failed spectacularly. Some even decided to join the Federation when it formed - we’ve got a few scout companies of mixed myr and nyrea. The ones that can take their minds off fucking for long enough to be useful, anyway.”
rows.translation: 莉芙点点头。“战争爆发前，联邦军队主要负责击退尼瑞亚的袭击。在我们的领土上，尼瑞亚拥有几个规模颇大的城邦。某位野心勃勃的女王甚至试图建立一个尼瑞亚国家，不过最后败得十分难看。联邦成立时，有些尼瑞亚甚至决定加入——我们有几个由米尔和尼瑞亚混编的侦察连。当然，前提是她们能暂时不去想着交配，发挥一点实际作用。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve nods. “Before the war, Federation troops were mainly fighting off nyrea raids. Back in our territory, the nyrea have a few fairly large city-states. One particularly ambitious queen even tried to form a nyrean country, though that failed spectacularly. Some even decided to join the Federation when it formed - we’ve got a few scout companies of mixed myr and nyrea. The ones that can take their minds off fucking for long enough to be useful, anyway.”"

rows.original: “Speaking of minds full of fucking, you’ll want to keep clear of any myr - of any color - you find out there. The ones that aren’t deserters looking to steal from you are likely to be infested with the myrmedius fungus. I don’t know what it would do to an offworlder, but to myr, it drives us mad with lust. Infected victims can be unpredictable, and will try to force themselves on you. They’re not particularly physically strong, but can still get the better of you if you aren’t careful.”
rows.translation: “说到满脑子交配，你最好避开在那里遇到的任何米尔——不管什么颜色。她们不是想偷你东西的逃兵，就很可能感染了米尔梅迪乌斯真菌。我不知道它会对外星人造成什么影响，但对米尔而言，它会让我们因欲望而发疯。受感染者的行为难以预测，还会试图强迫你。她们的身体并不特别强壮，不过你若不谨慎，依然可能栽在她们手里。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Speaking of minds full of fucking, you’ll want to keep clear of any myr - of any color - you find out there. The ones that aren’t deserters looking to steal from you are likely to be infested with the myrmedius fungus. I don’t know what it would do to an offworlder, but to myr, it drives us mad with lust. Infected victims can be unpredictable, and will try to force themselves on you. They’re not particularly physically strong, but can still get the better of you if you aren’t careful.”"

rows.original: You ask how to recognize an infected myr, to which Lieve answers, “You’ll see them, believe me. They’re surrounded by spore clouds, and the fungus grows all over them. It’s... not pleasant to look at.”
rows.translation: 你询问该如何辨认受感染的米尔，莉芙回答：“你看到就会知道，相信我。她们周围笼罩着孢子云，真菌长满全身。那副样子...可不好看。”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou ask how to recognize an infected myr, to which Lieve answers, “You’ll see them, believe me. They’re surrounded by spore clouds, and the fungus grows all over them. It’s... not pleasant to look at.”"

rows.original: “Anything else I should be aware of?”
rows.translation: “还有什么需要注意的吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Anything else I should be aware of?”"

rows.original: “There are other creatures out there, but the nyrea and fungal myr are the most common in No Myrs’s. If you go down in the deep caves, you’ll start seeing wetraxxal and creatures made of a living goo called the ganrael. Any of them can be bad news. Stay clear of them if you can. If not, well, I hope you’re as tough as you look.”
rows.translation: “那里还有其他生物，不过尼瑞亚和真菌感染的米尔在无米尔之地最为常见。要是进入深层洞穴，你会开始遇到维特拉克塞尔，还有一种叫加恩雷尔、由活体黏胶构成的生物。它们没一个是好消息。能躲就躲，躲不开的话，希望你有看上去那么强悍。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“There are other creatures out there, but the nyrea and fungal myr are the most common in No Myrs’s. If you go down in the deep caves, you’ll start seeing wetraxxal and creatures made of a living goo called the ganrael. Any of them can be bad news. Stay clear of them if you can. If not, well, I hope you’re as tough as you look.”"

rows.original: No Man’s Land
rows.translation: 无人之地
rows.raw: "No Man’s Land"

rows.original: No Myr’s Land
rows.translation: 无米尔之地
rows.raw: "No Myr’s Land"

rows.original: Ask for details about the stretch of territory outside Kressia: No Myr’s Land.
rows.translation: 询问有关克雷西亚城外那片领土的详情：无米尔之地。
rows.raw: "Ask for details about the stretch of territory outside Kressia: No Myr’s Land."

rows.original: Fungal Myr
rows.translation: 真菌米尔
rows.raw: "Fungal Myr"

rows.original: Fungal Myr
rows.translation: 真菌米尔
rows.raw: "Fungal Myr"

rows.original: Try and get more information about the fungus-infected myr.
rows.translation: 试着进一步了解那些感染真菌的米尔。
rows.raw: "Try and get more information about the fungus-infected myr."

rows.original: Fungal Myr
rows.translation: 真菌米尔
rows.raw: "Fungal Myr"

rows.original: The War
rows.translation: 战争
rows.raw: "The War"

rows.original: “What can you tell me about the war?” you ask.
rows.translation: “你能跟我讲讲这场战争吗？”你问道。
rows.raw: "“What can you tell me about the war?” you ask."

rows.original: “If you don’t mind me asking.”
rows.translation: “如果你不介意我问的话。”
rows.raw: " “If you don’t mind me asking.”"

rows.original: Lieve sighs and scratches her head, just under one of her antennae. “I can tell you you’d be better off asking one of my commanders. Colonel Nehzara loves briefing offworlders, I’m sure.”
rows.translation: 莉芙叹了口气，在一根触角下方挠了挠头。“我只能告诉你，去问我的某位指挥官会更好。内扎拉上校很喜欢给外星人介绍情况，我敢肯定。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve sighs and scratches her head, just under one of her antennae. “I can tell you you’d be better off asking one of my commanders. Colonel Nehzara loves briefing offworlders, I’m sure.”"

rows.original: That may be so, but you’d still like to hear Lieve’s take on things. She grunts at the prompting, rolling her eyes. “Alright, alright. What do you want to know?”
rows.translation: 也许确实如此，但你还是想听听莉芙的看法。在你的催促下，她哼了一声，翻了个白眼。“好吧，好吧。你想知道什么？”
rows.raw: "\n\nThat may be so, but you’d still like to hear Lieve’s take on things. She grunts at the prompting, rolling her eyes. “Alright, alright. What do you want to know?”"

rows.original: “Let’s start with how it began.”
rows.translation: “先说说它是怎么开始的吧。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Let’s start with how it began.”"

rows.original: “We’ve been in conflict with the golds for generations. You need to understand that. They thought we were rogue hives they could push around, and we pushed back every time. But they were always small things: a few shots across the border, a few cargo ships raided. It was bad, but not war bad. Finally, the golds forced our hand,” Lieve says, quickly replacing her hesitance on the topic with vitriol. “They were testing new military aircraft, flew ‘em right into our territory. Our air corps intercepted them, tried to escort them back to neutral territory. Instead, the goldies opened fire, turned it into the first full-on dogfight in Myrellion’s history. Right over a populated city, too. If that’s not a declaration of war, I don’t know what is.”
rows.translation: “我们和金族冲突了好几代人。你得先明白这一点。她们觉得我们是可以任意摆布的离群蜂巢，而我们每次都会反击。不过以前都是些小事：边境上开几枪，劫几艘货船。情况很糟，但还没糟到称得上战争。最后，是金族逼得我们不得不动手，”莉芙说道，谈及此事时的迟疑迅速被怨毒取代。“她们在测试新型军用飞机，直接飞进了我们的领土。我们的空军拦截她们，试图护送她们返回中立领空。结果金鬼子反而开了火，把事情变成米瑞利昂历史上第一场全面空战。而且就在一座人口稠密的城市上空。要这还不算宣战，我就不知道什么才算了。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“We’ve been in conflict with the golds for generations. You need to understand that. They thought we were rogue hives they could push around, and we pushed back every time. But they were always small things: a few shots across the border, a few cargo ships raided. It was bad, but not war bad. Finally, the golds forced our hand,” Lieve says, quickly replacing her hesitance on the topic with vitriol. “They were testing new military aircraft, flew ‘em right into our territory. Our air corps intercepted them, tried to escort them back to neutral territory. Instead, the goldies opened fire, turned it into the first full-on dogfight in Myrellion’s history. Right over a populated city, too. If that’s not a declaration of war, I don’t know what is.”"

rows.original: You cock an eye at that. “The golds just attacked you? Out of the blue like that?”
rows.translation: 你对此挑起眉毛。“金族就这么袭击了你们？毫无征兆？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou cock an eye at that. “The golds just attacked you? Out of the blue like that?”"

rows.original: She shrugs. “I guess. They say it was a mistake, but you don’t fly a squadron that far out of your territory for no reason. Not in your fancy new fighter planes, and not in spitting distance of one of our airbases. They wanted a fight, and we gave them one.”
rows.translation: 她耸耸肩。“大概吧。她们说那是个误会，可你不会无缘无故让整支中队飞到离本国领土那么远的地方。更不会开着崭新的先进战斗机，飞到我们一座空军基地近在咫尺的位置。她们想打，我们就奉陪了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe shrugs. “I guess. They say it was a mistake, but you don’t fly a squadron that far out of your territory for no reason. Not in your fancy new fighter planes, and not in spitting distance of one of our airbases. They wanted a fight, and we gave them one.”"

rows.original: A quick glance down shows both of Lieve’s wives seem to be chafing at her comments, but they clearly know better than to speak up about it.
rows.translation: 你低头匆匆一瞥，发现莉芙的两位妻子似乎都对她的言论感到不自在，但她们显然很清楚最好别开口。
rows.raw: "\n\nA quick glance down shows both of Lieve’s wives seem to be chafing at her comments, but they clearly know better than to speak up about it."

rows.original: “Federation and the Republic were at war inside a week. We came down on the golds like a hammer - harder than they could have ever expected. Their bases on our continent didn’t know what hit them. It’s been seven years of pushing over the northern deserts, across the ocean, and into the tunnels since then.”
rows.translation: “不到一周，联邦和共和国便开战了。我们像重锤般砸向金族——攻势之猛远超她们想象。她们在我们大陆上的基地根本还没反应过来。此后的七年里，我们一路推进，越过北部沙漠、横跨海洋，最后打进了隧道。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Federation and the Republic were at war inside a week. We came down on the golds like a hammer - harder than they could have ever expected. Their bases on our continent didn’t know what hit them. It’s been seven years of pushing over the northern deserts, across the ocean, and into the tunnels since then.”"

rows.original: Seven years. Must have been brutal - most of the wars you hear about in U.G.C. space don’t last a year. Too costly by far. After a moment’s thought, you ask, “When did you join the military?”
rows.translation: 七年。肯定惨烈至极——你听说过的联星会星域战争大多持续不了一年，代价实在太高。思索片刻后，你问道：“你是什么时候参军的？”
rows.raw: "\n\nSeven years. Must have been brutal - most of the wars you hear about in U.G.C. space don’t last a year. Too costly by far. After a moment’s thought, you ask, “When did you join the military?”"

rows.original: “Four years ago,” Lieve answers, the venom fading from her speech just as easily as it came. “I wasn’t old enough to sign up for Federal service when the fighting started. Didn’t stop me from trying to help, though. After the war went hot, just about every girl in Federation territory signed up for physical fitness, survival training, anything we could get to toughen us up until it was our turn to enlist. I joined a martial arts school, and pulled shifts in a munitions factory in the city whenever I could.”
rows.translation: “四年前，”莉芙答道，话语中的怨毒来得快去得也一样快。“战斗开始时，我还没到能报名参加联邦服役的年龄。但这并没阻止我尽力帮忙。战争全面爆发后，联邦领土上几乎所有姑娘都报名参加了体能训练、生存训练，能让我们强健起来、撑到应征那天的训练都参加。我进了一所武术学校，一有机会就在城里的军火厂轮班。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Four years ago,” Lieve answers, the venom fading from her speech just as easily as it came. “I wasn’t old enough to sign up for Federal service when the fighting started. Didn’t stop me from trying to help, though. After the war went hot, just about every girl in Federation territory signed up for physical fitness, survival training, anything we could get to toughen us up until it was our turn to enlist. I joined a martial arts school, and pulled shifts in a munitions factory in the city whenever I could.”"

rows.original: “In the city?” you ask. The way she says it makes it sound almost foreign to her.
rows.translation: “城里？”你问道。她说这个词的语气，仿佛那地方对她而言几乎是异乡。
rows.raw: "\n\n“In the city?” you ask. The way she says it makes it sound almost foreign to her."

rows.original: She nods, and you could swear you can see a bit of blush creep into her cheeks as she answers, “I didn’t grow up in a city. My parents had a fungus farm, deep underground. Not big enough to be one of High Command’s breadbaskets, but we did what we could. Any, uh, anyway, when it was my year, I enlisted as soon as I could.”
rows.translation: 她点点头，你敢发誓能看见一抹红晕爬上她的脸颊。她回答道：“我不是在城市里长大的。我父母在地底深处经营一座真菌农场。规模没大到能成为最高司令部的粮仓之一，但我们也尽了自己的力。总、总之，轮到我的那一年，我一到年龄就立刻入伍了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe nods, and you could swear you can see a bit of blush creep into her cheeks as she answers, “I didn’t grow up in a city. My parents had a fungus farm, deep underground. Not big enough to be one of High Command’s breadbaskets, but we did what we could. Any, uh, anyway, when it was my year, I enlisted as soon as I could.”"

rows.original: All the red myr sounded eager to fight, the way Lieve describes it. You ask her if everyone in the Federation jumped at the chance to fight like she did.
rows.translation: 照莉芙的描述，所有红米尔似乎都渴望战斗。你问她，联邦里的每个人是否都像她一样迫不及待地抓住了参战机会。
rows.raw: "\n\nAll the red myr sounded eager to fight, the way Lieve describes it. You ask her if everyone in the Federation jumped at the chance to fight like she did."

rows.original: <i>“Most did, yeah. We’re not like the golds, Steele - they barely had a proper military when the war started, had to draft year after year. In the Federation,
rows.translation: <i>“大多数人都这样，没错。我们和金族不一样，斯蒂尔——战争开始时，她们几乎连一支像样的军队都没有，只能年复一年地征兵。在联邦，
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“Most did, yeah. We’re not like the golds, Steele - they barely had a proper military when the war started, had to draft year after year. In the Federation,"

rows.original: service guarantees citizenship
rows.translation: 服役就能保证获得公民权
rows.raw: " service guarantees citizenship"

rows.original: you can only get full citizenship and the right to vote through military service
rows.translation: 只有通过服兵役，才能取得完整公民权和投票权
rows.raw: " you can only get full citizenship and the right to vote through military service"

rows.original: . Even in peacetime, serving is a sacred duty for most myr, at least for a few years. We lived in a much, much rougher part of the world than the golds did, always under threat from monsters coming down from the north. When the war kicked off, the Federation had plenty of veteran soldiers ready to lead the vanguard, and more volunteers than it could handle.”
rows.translation: 。即使在和平时期，对大多数米尔来说，服役也是神圣的义务，至少得服上几年。我们生活的地区比金族那里严酷得多，始终面临着从北方南下的怪物威胁。战争爆发时，联邦有许多经验丰富的老兵可以带领先锋部队，志愿者的数量更是多得应付不过来。”
rows.raw: ". Even in peacetime, serving is a sacred duty for most myr, at least for a few years. We lived in a much, much rougher part of the world than the golds did, always under threat from monsters coming down from the north. When the war kicked off, the Federation had plenty of veteran soldiers ready to lead the vanguard, and more volunteers than it could handle.”"

rows.original: “And the war went well for you?”
rows.translation: “所以战争对你们很顺利？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“And the war went well for you?”"

rows.original: Lieve grins proudly. “It did. As you might have guessed from us sitting in Kressia, a golden city, just outside the gold capital. There were rough spots, of course. Especially when the golds went for chemical weapons - nobody was prepared for that. Bad couple of years since then, but we still pushed on. They put up a good fight, but once we managed to land on the continent, well, there wasn’t much they could do to stop us.”
rows.translation: 莉芙自豪地咧嘴一笑。“很顺利。你大概也猜到了，毕竟我们现在就坐在克雷西亚——一座金族城市，距离金族首都也不远。当然，战况也有过艰难的时候。尤其是金族开始使用化学武器之后——没人对此有所准备。那之后有几年很不好过，但我们还是继续推进。她们顽强抵抗过，可我们一旦成功登陆那片大陆，她们就没什么办法阻止我们了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve grins proudly. “It did. As you might have guessed from us sitting in Kressia, a golden city, just outside the gold capital. There were rough spots, of course. Especially when the golds went for chemical weapons - nobody was prepared for that. Bad couple of years since then, but we still pushed on. They put up a good fight, but once we managed to land on the continent, well, there wasn’t much they could do to stop us.”"

rows.original: You can’t suppress a mischievous smirk as you ask,
rows.translation: 你压不住促狭的坏笑，问道：
rows.raw: "You can’t suppress a mischievous smirk as you ask, "

rows.original: “What did stop you, then?”
rows.translation: “那后来究竟是什么阻止了你们？”
rows.raw: "“What did stop you, then?”"

rows.original: Lieve’s grin twists into a scowl. “You offworlders showing up for one thing! The war would be over if your ships had just showed up a day later.”
rows.translation: 莉芙的笑容扭成了怒容。“首先就是你们这些外星人来了！你们的飞船要是晚一天出现，战争早就结束了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve’s grin twists into a scowl. “You offworlders showing up for one thing! The war would be over if your ships had just showed up a day later.”"

rows.original: “We’d all be dead, too, Lieve,” Sierva adds, earning a sharp look from her mistress.
rows.translation: “那我们也都会死，莉芙，”希尔瓦补充道，惹得女主人狠狠瞪了她一眼。
rows.raw: "\n\n“We’d all be dead, too, Lieve,” Sierva adds, earning a sharp look from her mistress."

rows.original: Lieve grumbles something under her breath, but admits, “Yeah, that too. But it would be the Federation left standing in the end: you may have gotten nukes, too, but even then you wouldn’t have been able to get them across the ocean.”
rows.translation: 莉芙低声嘟囔了几句，不过还是承认：“对，还有这事。但最后站着的会是联邦：你们也许同样造出了核弹，可就算如此，也不可能把它们送到大洋彼岸。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve grumbles something under her breath, but admits, “Yeah, that too. But it would be the Federation left standing in the end: you may have gotten nukes, too, but even then you wouldn’t have been able to get them across the ocean.”"

rows.original: Sierva shrugs at that, and Lieve adds, “She’s right, though. High Command was going to drill nukes into Gildenmere. It would have been... bad... but High Command says we’d lose fewer troops that way than trying a ground assault.”
rows.translation: 希尔瓦对此耸耸肩，莉芙补充道：“不过她说得对。最高司令部本来打算把核弹钻进吉尔登米尔。那会变得...非常糟糕...但最高司令部说，这样牺牲的部队会比发动地面进攻更少。”
rows.raw: "\n\nSierva shrugs at that, and Lieve adds, “She’s right, though. High Command was going to drill nukes into Gildenmere. It would have been... bad... but High Command says we’d lose fewer troops that way than trying a ground assault.”"

rows.original: “I’m glad you space-people came to save us!” Mayren adds with a dopey smile. Lieve just rolls her eyes.
rows.translation: “我很高兴你们这些太空人来救了我们！”梅伦傻笑着补充道。莉芙只是翻了个白眼。
rows.raw: "\n\n“I’m glad you space-people came to save us!” Mayren adds with a dopey smile. Lieve just rolls her eyes."

rows.raw: "Ask Lieve about those brutal scars on her back."

rows.original: Trench Wives
rows.translation: 战壕妻子
rows.raw: "Trench Wives"

rows.original: “Tell me about these two,” you prompt, nodding to the gold myr girls clinging to Lieve. “How does a red myr soldier end up with a couple of gold girls hanging on her like that?”
rows.translation: “跟我说说她们俩吧，”你指着依偎在莉芙身旁的金米尔姑娘，提示道。“一个红米尔士兵怎么会有两个金族姑娘这样缠在身边？”
rows.raw: "“Tell me about these two,” you prompt, nodding to the gold myr girls clinging to Lieve. “How does a red myr soldier end up with a couple of gold girls hanging on her like that?”"

rows.original: “With my winning personality, mostly,” Lieve chuckles, running her hand through one of the girls’ hair. “Well, and winning the war, too.”
rows.translation: “主要靠我迷人的个性，”莉芙轻笑着，用手梳过其中一名姑娘的头发。“嗯，还有打赢战争。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“With my winning personality, mostly,” Lieve chuckles, running her hand through one of the girls’ hair. “Well, and winning the war, too.”"

rows.original: You urge Lieve on, and she most happily obliges. “Trench wives are prisoners of war. We’ve taken more prisoners than we could ever possibly deal with over the last seven years. Thousands and thousands of deserters we’ve picked up, wounded we’ve pulled out of No Myr’s Land, and more surrendered soldiers than we could stuff into camps even if we wanted to. But P.O.W.s have to go somewhere, right?”
rows.translation: 你催促莉芙继续说，她十分乐意地照办了。“战壕妻子都是战俘。过去七年里，我们俘虏的人多得根本处理不过来。我们收容了成千上万名逃兵，从无米尔之地救回无数伤员，还有多得就算想塞进战俘营也塞不下的投降士兵。但战俘总得有个去处，对吧？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou urge Lieve on, and she most happily obliges. “Trench wives are prisoners of war. We’ve taken more prisoners than we could ever possibly deal with over the last seven years. Thousands and thousands of deserters we’ve picked up, wounded we’ve pulled out of No Myr’s Land, and more surrendered soldiers than we could stuff into camps even if we wanted to. But P.O.W.s have to go somewhere, right?”"

rows.original: “Somewhere being your bed?”
rows.translation: “那个去处就是你的床？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Somewhere being your bed?”"

rows.original: Lieve flashes you a slight twitch of a smile. “That’s the idea. High Command doesn’t have the resources to deal with so many prisoners even if they wanted to. We’d have half the army relegated to guard duty that way, not to mention the food, space, shelter. From what I’ve heard, they realized the problem was going to be catastrophic before the first year of the war was over. So officers started telling their troops to keep prisoners for themselves, like in ancient days. To the victor goes the spoils, right?”
rows.translation: 莉芙唇角微微一动。“就是这个意思。即使最高司令部想处理这么多俘虏，也没有足够资源。要是那么做，半支军队都得转去看守她们，更别提食物、空间和住所了。据我所知，战争第一年还没结束，她们就意识到这个问题会变成灾难。于是军官开始让士兵把俘虏留给自己，就像古代那样。战利品归胜者，对吧？”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve flashes you a slight twitch of a smile. “That’s the idea. High Command doesn’t have the resources to deal with so many prisoners even if they wanted to. We’d have half the army relegated to guard duty that way, not to mention the food, space, shelter. From what I’ve heard, they realized the problem was going to be catastrophic before the first year of the war was over. So officers started telling their troops to keep prisoners for themselves, like in ancient days. To the victor goes the spoils, right?”"

rows.original: That’s certainly one way to look at it.
rows.translation: 这确实是一种看待问题的方式。
rows.raw: "\n\nThat’s certainly one way to look at it."

rows.original: Though it is somewhat... primitive.
rows.translation: 尽管多少有些...原始。
rows.raw: " Though it is somewhat... primitive."

rows.original: It certainly seems to be working out for Lieve.
rows.translation: 这办法对莉芙而言显然相当奏效。
rows.raw: " It certainly seems to be working out for Lieve."

rows.original: One you can certainly respect.
rows.translation: 也是一种你当然可以尊重的做法。
rows.raw: " One you can certainly respect."

rows.original: Lieve smirks. “It’s not exactly barbaric. We take care of them, and in return, they take care of our needs. It’s a lot better than the alternatives.”
rows.translation: 莉芙得意一笑。“这也不算野蛮。我们照顾她们，作为回报，她们满足我们的需求。总比其他选择好得多。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve smirks. “It’s not exactly barbaric. We take care of them, and in return, they take care of our needs. It’s a lot better than the alternatives.”"

rows.original: “It could be worse,” Sierva says, reclining against the wall. “I’d rather be at home, well fed and wrapped up in my robes and a warm bed... but anything’s better than dead.”
rows.translation: “还可能更糟，”希尔瓦靠着墙说道。“我更想待在家里，吃得饱饱的，裹着长袍躺在暖床上...但总比死了强。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“It could be worse,” Sierva says, reclining against the wall. “I’d rather be at home, well fed and wrapped up in my robes and a warm bed... but anything’s better than dead.”"

rows.original: May pipes up, adding, “Or fighting! I’d rather eat pussy all day long than have to get shot at all the time.”
rows.translation: 梅伦插话道：“或者上战场！我宁愿整天舔骚屄，也不想老是挨枪子。”
rows.raw: "\n\nMay pipes up, adding, “Or fighting! I’d rather eat pussy all day long than have to get shot at all the time.”"

rows.original: Lieve snickers and ruffles the honeypot’s golden hair.
rows.translation: 莉芙嗤笑一声，揉乱了蜜乳娘的金发。
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve snickers and ruffles the honeypot’s golden hair."

rows.original: You’re not sure if it’s honest affection between the three of them, or the lingering addiction to myr venom that makes the two gold myr respond that way.
rows.translation: 你不确定她们三人之间是否真有感情，又或者只是米尔毒液残留的成瘾性让两名金米尔作出这种反应。
rows.raw: " You’re not sure if it’s honest affection between the three of them, or the lingering addiction to myr venom that makes the two gold myr respond that way."

rows.original: “And how does one acquire a harem like this?” you ask, nodding towards the golden girls at Lieve’s feet.
rows.translation: “那要怎么才能得到这样一座后宫？”你问道，朝莉芙脚边的金族姑娘们点了点头。
rows.raw: "\n\n“And how does one acquire a harem like this?” you ask, nodding towards the golden girls at Lieve’s feet."

rows.original: “Oh, a little violence, a little luck...” Lieve grins, patting the hatchet slung on her hip. “Every harem’s different. Some are awarded by officers to particularly brave or heroic soldiers; others are accumulated over time. Capture an enemy officer here, lead the charge on an enemy base there, maybe find a wounded beauty dying in a foxhole.”
rows.translation: “哦，一点暴力，一点运气...”莉芙咧嘴一笑，拍了拍挂在腰间的短柄斧。“每座后宫都不一样。有些由军官奖给格外勇敢或英勇的士兵；另一些则是日积月累攒起来的。在这里俘虏一名敌军军官，在那里带队冲锋一座敌军基地，也许还能发现一个奄奄一息躺在散兵坑里的美人。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Oh, a little violence, a little luck...” Lieve grins, patting the hatchet slung on her hip. “Every harem’s different. Some are awarded by officers to particularly brave or heroic soldiers; others are accumulated over time. Capture an enemy officer here, lead the charge on an enemy base there, maybe find a wounded beauty dying in a foxhole.”"

rows.original: She flashes Sierva a little smile.
rows.translation: 她朝希尔瓦微微一笑。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe flashes Sierva a little smile."

rows.original: Trench Wives
rows.translation: 战壕妻子
rows.raw: "Trench Wives"

rows.translation: 战壕妻子
rows.raw: "Trench Wives"

rows.translation: 询问莉芙的后宫，以及战壕妻子的一般情况。
rows.raw: "Ask about Lieve’s harem, and Trench Wives in general."

rows.original: Fed.Army
rows.translation: 联邦军队
rows.raw: "Fed.Army"

rows.original: You ask Lieve to tell you a little bit about the Federation’s military. After all, that seems to be the organization that you’re primarily interacting with here in Kressia.
rows.translation: 你请莉芙稍微讲讲联邦军队。毕竟，你在克雷西亚主要打交道的似乎就是这个组织。
rows.raw: "You ask Lieve to tell you a little bit about the Federation’s military. After all, that seems to be the organization that you’re primarily interacting with here in Kressia."

rows.original: “I’d say it’s like any other army, but I don’t exactly know how you aliens do it. Aside from the whole trucking into orbit like you own the place - that was surprisingly familiar. But, uh, really we’re fairly simple in structure. Just like the civilian government, we’re all ultimately answerable to High Command. That’s a group of generals that we veterans elect to run the Federation, make all the important decisions. Under them, we’ve got the individual armies and the generals who don’t rate getting on the High Command board. We’re broken up into... you weren’t asking about our organizational structure, were you?”
rows.translation: “我想它和其他军队都差不多，可我也不清楚你们外星人是怎么做的。除了像这里本来就是你们家一样整批闯进轨道——这点意外地熟悉。不过，呃，我们的结构其实相当简单。和文职政府一样，我们最终都向最高司令部负责。那是由一群经我们这些老兵选举产生的将军组成，负责管理联邦、作出所有重大决定。她们下面是各支军队，以及那些级别不够进入最高司令部委员会的将军。我们分成了...你不是在问我们的组织结构，对吧？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I’d say it’s like any other army, but I don’t exactly know how you aliens do it. Aside from the whole trucking into orbit like you own the place - that was surprisingly familiar. But, uh, really we’re fairly simple in structure. Just like the civilian government, we’re all ultimately answerable to High Command. That’s a group of generals that we veterans elect to run the Federation, make all the important decisions. Under them, we’ve got the individual armies and the generals who don’t rate getting on the High Command board. We’re broken up into... you weren’t asking about our organizational structure, were you?”"

rows.original: You confess that you were more interested in the more intimate details.
rows.translation: 你承认，自己对更私密的细节更感兴趣。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou confess that you were more interested in the more intimate details."

rows.original: “Well,” Lieve says. “Let’s start with the basics. We train for a period of six weeks, twelve if you’re selected to be an officer or specialist like a radioman or a minesweeper. Basic training is almost all about discipline: making sure we know how to follow orders, how to stay calm under fire and keep your wits about you. That discipline is more important than even fighting skill, when you get right down to it. Federation troops don’t panic when the shells start flying, or when the enemy comes up out of their trenches. The girls we’ve recruited the last few years are even trained for gas and chemical attacks.”
rows.translation: “好吧，”莉芙说道。“从基础讲起。我们训练六周，如果被选为军官，或是无线电员、扫雷兵之类的专业人员，就要训练十二周。基础训练几乎全在培养纪律：确保我们懂得如何服从命令，如何在炮火下保持镇定、头脑清醒。说到底，这种纪律甚至比战斗技巧更重要。炮弹开始落下，或敌人从战壕里冲出来时，联邦部队不会惊慌。过去几年征募的姑娘甚至接受过应对毒气和化学袭击的训练。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Well,” Lieve says. “Let’s start with the basics. We train for a period of six weeks, twelve if you’re selected to be an officer or specialist like a radioman or a minesweeper. Basic training is almost all about discipline: making sure we know how to follow orders, how to stay calm under fire and keep your wits about you. That discipline is more important than even fighting skill, when you get right down to it. Federation troops don’t panic when the shells start flying, or when the enemy comes up out of their trenches. The girls we’ve recruited the last few years are even trained for gas and chemical attacks.”"

rows.original: “I’m sure that doesn’t seem like much to you off-worlders, but there’s a hell of a difference between a Federation soldier who’s been drilled to perfection and a gold who’s just been conscripted and had a rifle shoved in her hands for the first time ten minutes before they throw her over the top. There’s nothing more important than discipline, training, and experience for surviving in the trenches when you’re getting shot at and shelled for weeks on end. Basic can give you two of them, at least.”
rows.translation: “我知道，对你们外星人来说这也许不算什么，但一名千锤百炼的联邦士兵，和一个才被征召、在被赶出战壕十分钟前第一次拿到步枪的金族，完全是天壤之别。当你一连数周在战壕里挨枪挨炮时，没有什么比纪律、训练和经验更能让你活下来。至少基础训练能给你其中两样。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I’m sure that doesn’t seem like much to you off-worlders, but there’s a hell of a difference between a Federation soldier who’s been drilled to perfection and a gold who’s just been conscripted and had a rifle shoved in her hands for the first time ten minutes before they throw her over the top. There’s nothing more important than discipline, training, and experience for surviving in the trenches when you’re getting shot at and shelled for weeks on end. Basic can give you two of them, at least.”"

rows.original: Curious, you ask if there’s much more to Federation service than fighting in the trenches.
rows.translation: 出于好奇，你问联邦服役除了在战壕中作战外，是否还有许多其他工作。
rows.raw: "\n\nCurious, you ask if there’s much more to Federation service than fighting in the trenches."

rows.original: “Depends on your aptitudes,” Lieve answers with a shrug. “Girls with technical aptitude, good typists, scientists, anybody with useful skills usually get selected for special service. An army needs a lot of pencil pushers, and there’s thousands of girls working in R&D. We weren’t the first to get nukes by chance, you know. Of course, the position everybody wants these days is to be a fly girl with the air corps. Most of us had never seen the surface before the war, and now we’re sending hundreds of troops into the sky. One step closer to having ourselves a space corps, just like you offworlders.”
rows.translation: “看你的天赋，”莉芙耸耸肩答道。“擅长技术的姑娘、打字员、科学家，任何拥有实用技能的人通常都会入选特别勤务。军队需要大量文职人员，还有成千上万的姑娘在研发部门工作。我们最先造出核弹可不是靠运气。当然，如今人人都想进空军当飞行姑娘。战争前，我们大多数人从没见过地表，现在却正把数百名士兵送上天空。离建立一支像你们外星人那样的太空军又近了一步。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Depends on your aptitudes,” Lieve answers with a shrug. “Girls with technical aptitude, good typists, scientists, anybody with useful skills usually get selected for special service. An army needs a lot of pencil pushers, and there’s thousands of girls working in R&D. We weren’t the first to get nukes by chance, you know. Of course, the position everybody wants these days is to be a fly girl with the air corps. Most of us had never seen the surface before the war, and now we’re sending hundreds of troops into the sky. One step closer to having ourselves a space corps, just like you offworlders.”"
