rows.original: Citizenship
rows.translation: 公民权
rows.raw: "Citizenship"

rows.original: Ask Lieve about Federal Citizenship. From what you understand, it’s very different from how the Confederate government handles things.
rows.translation: 向莉芙询问联邦公民权。据你所知，它和邦联政府处理此事的方式截然不同。
rows.raw: "Ask Lieve about Federal Citizenship. From what you understand, it’s very different from how the Confederate government handles things."

rows.original: Red Myr Blood
rows.raw: "Red Myr Blood"

rows.original: Blood Sample
rows.translation: 血液样本
rows.raw: "Blood Sample"

rows.original: Surely Lieve can see the benefit of helping out the Xenogen scientists. A myr gene mod for her race would certainly spike the popularity of the reds among offworlders, and get Xenogen on her side. As diplomatically as you can, you ask the perky ant-girl if she wouldn’t mind donating a little blood to the cause.
rows.translation: 莉芙肯定能看出帮助异源生物科技科学家的好处。为她的种族开发一种米尔基因改造剂，必然会让红族在外星人中大受欢迎，也会让异源生物科技站到她这边。你尽可能委婉地问这位活泼的蚁女是否介意为此捐一点血。
rows.raw: "Surely Lieve can see the benefit of helping out the Xenogen scientists. A myr gene mod for her race would certainly spike the popularity of the reds among offworlders, and get Xenogen on her side. As diplomatically as you can, you ask the perky ant-girl if she wouldn’t mind donating a little blood to the cause."

rows.original: “Blood?” Lieve echoes, cocking an eyebrow at you. “What do scientists need my blood for?”
rows.translation: “血？”莉芙重复道，朝你挑起一边眉毛。“科学家要我的血做什么？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Blood?” Lieve echoes, cocking an eyebrow at you. “What do scientists need my blood for?”"

rows.original: “For, like, science and stuff!” you answer giddily. “They wanna help people like me be more like you!”
rows.translation: “为了，那个，科学什么的！”你兴奋地回答。“她们想帮我这样的人变得更像你！”
rows.raw: "“For, like, science and stuff!” you answer giddily. “They wanna help people like me be more like you!”"

rows.original: “They want to make a gene-mod that’ll turn people like me into gold and red myr. The Xenogen scientists just need some samples from a red myr like you to finish it.”
rows.translation: “她们想制造一种基因改造剂，把我这样的人变成金米尔和红米尔。异源生物科技的科学家只需要你这样一名红米尔提供些样本，就能完成它。”
rows.raw: "“They want to make a gene-mod that’ll turn people like me into gold and red myr. The Xenogen scientists just need some samples from a red myr like you to finish it.”"

rows.original: “Your scientists can do that? Really? That’s... even more amazing than the medicine they gave us after the war ended,” Lieve says. “So you offworlders really can just... change whatever race you are? I’d heard that, but I’m not sure I ever really believed it.”
rows.translation: “你们的科学家能做到这种事？真的？这...甚至比战争结束后她们给我们的药还不可思议，”莉芙说道。“所以你们外星人真的可以...随意改变自己的种族？我听说过这件事，但不确定自己是否真正相信过。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Your scientists can do that? Really? That’s... even more amazing than the medicine they gave us after the war ended,” Lieve says. “So you offworlders really can just... change whatever race you are? I’d heard that, but I’m not sure I ever really believed it.”"

rows.original: You assure her that they can, and that a few droplets of her blood - plus maybe a few strands of hair and flakes of skin for good measure - could help make sure there’s a galaxy full of wanna-be reds in no time.
rows.translation: 你向她保证，她们确实能做到；几滴她的血——或许再加几缕头发和一些皮屑以防万一——很快就能确保银河系里到处都是想成为红族的人。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou assure her that they can, and that a few droplets of her blood - plus maybe a few strands of hair and flakes of skin for good measure - could help make sure there’s a galaxy full of wanna-be reds in no time."

rows.original: She grins. “Well, when you put it like that... I guess I ought to help you, huh? It’s practically my patriotic duty.”
rows.translation: 她咧嘴笑了。“嗯，既然你都这么说了...我想自己应该帮忙，对吧？这几乎是我的爱国义务。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe grins. “Well, when you put it like that... I guess I ought to help you, huh? It’s practically my patriotic duty.”"

rows.original: Now that’s the spirit. Lieve pulls the hatchet off of her belt and makes quick work of drawing its blade across one of her fingers. She squeezes several droplets of blood into a vial you hand her before tasking Mayren to go fetch her a bandage. You put a cap on the vial and flash Lieve a smile. Giving her your thanks, you flip the vial into your pack, ready to be delivered to Nevrie back at the DMZ.
rows.translation: 这才对嘛。莉芙从腰带上取下短柄斧，干脆利落地用斧刃划过一根手指。她把几滴血挤进你递给她的小瓶，随后吩咐梅伦去给她拿绷带。你盖好瓶盖，朝莉芙微微一笑。道谢之后，你把小瓶抛进背包，准备交给非军事区的内芙莉。
rows.raw: "\n\nNow that’s the spirit. Lieve pulls the hatchet off of her belt and makes quick work of drawing its blade across one of her fingers. She squeezes several droplets of blood into a vial you hand her before tasking Mayren to go fetch her a bandage. You put a cap on the vial and flash Lieve a smile. Giving her your thanks, you flip the vial into your pack, ready to be delivered to Nevrie back at the DMZ."

rows.original: “Hard to believe that’s all it takes,” Lieve says with a chuckle, starting to wrap her finger up. “So, they’re going to be making transmutations for both myr races, aren’t they?”
rows.translation: “真难相信只需要这些，”莉芙轻笑着说道，开始包扎手指。“所以，她们会为两个米尔种族都制作转化剂，对吧？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Hard to believe that’s all it takes,” Lieve says with a chuckle, starting to wrap her finger up. “So, they’re going to be making transmutations for both myr races, aren’t they?”"

rows.original: You nod. That’s why you needed her blood, after all. They’re already working on one for the Golds.
rows.translation: 你点点头。毕竟这正是你需要她的血的原因。她们已经在为金族研制一种了。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou nod. That’s why you needed her blood, after all. They’re already working on one for the Golds."

rows.original: She nods thoughtfully. “I’m glad. I’ll be interested in seeing what they come up with.”
rows.translation: 她若有所思地点点头。“很好。我很想看看她们最后会做出什么。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe nods thoughtfully. “I’m glad. I’ll be interested in seeing what they come up with.”"

rows.original: With a teasing wink, she adds “Maybe I’ll see you as a hot little piece of red myr ass some day?”
rows.translation: 她调笑着眨了眨眼，又补充道：“也许有一天，我会看到你变成一块性感火辣的红米尔小翘臀？”
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a teasing wink, she adds “Maybe I’ll see you as a hot little piece of red myr ass some day?”"

rows.original: (Key Item Gained: Red Myr Blood)
rows.translation: (获得关键物品：红米尔血液)
rows.raw: "\n\n(Key Item Gained: Red Myr Blood)"

rows.original: Red Myr Blood
rows.raw: "Red Myr Blood"

rows.original: A vial of blood sampled from a red myr.
rows.translation: 一小瓶取自红米尔的血液样本。
rows.raw: "A vial of blood sampled from a red myr."

rows.original: Next
rows.translation: 下一步
rows.raw: "Next"

rows.original: Blood Sample
rows.translation: 血液样本
rows.raw: "Blood Sample"

rows.original: Ask Lieve if you could get a sample of her blood for Nevrie.
rows.translation: 问莉芙能否为内芙莉提供一份她的血液样本。
rows.raw: "Ask Lieve if you could get a sample of her blood for Nevrie."

rows.original: “Tell me about this... myrmedius fungus.”
rows.translation: “跟我说说这种...米尔梅迪乌斯真菌。”
rows.raw: "“Tell me about this... myrmedius fungus.”"

rows.original: Lieve shifts uncomfortably at the request, adjusting the collar of her uniform coat. “It’s a parasitic fungus that infects us myr, fuses to our nervous system and can alter our thoughts. It can cause lust-madness, forcing the victim to try and rampantly fuck anyone she can get her hands on. I’ve only ever seen one girl infected with it, and we had to flush her out of the camp. She’d tried to force herself on three privates, all in public. By the time the base guards got there, she was running around the parade ground begging anybody she could get her hands on to fuck her. She was crying the whole time, completely desperate. The poor thing must have been humiliated, but she couldn’t help herself.”
rows.translation: 莉芙听到请求后不自在地挪了挪身体，调整着制服外套的衣领。“它是一种会感染米尔的寄生真菌，能与我们的神经系统融合，并改变我们的思维。它会引起情欲癫狂，迫使受害者疯狂地和她能抓到的任何人交配。我只见过一个姑娘感染它，我们不得不把她赶出营地。她曾试图在大庭广众下强迫三名列兵。基地警卫赶到时，她正绕着阅兵场四处乱跑，乞求任何能抓到的人和她上床。她全程都在哭，彻底绝望。那可怜人肯定羞耻极了，但她控制不住自己。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve shifts uncomfortably at the request, adjusting the collar of her uniform coat. “It’s a parasitic fungus that infects us myr, fuses to our nervous system and can alter our thoughts. It can cause lust-madness, forcing the victim to try and rampantly fuck anyone she can get her hands on. I’ve only ever seen one girl infected with it, and we had to flush her out of the camp. She’d tried to force herself on three privates, all in public. By the time the base guards got there, she was running around the parade ground begging anybody she could get her hands on to fuck her. She was crying the whole time, completely desperate. The poor thing must have been humiliated, but she couldn’t help herself.”"

rows.original: That sounds awful.
rows.translation: 听起来糟透了。
rows.raw: "\n\nThat sounds awful."

rows.original: “It is,” Lieve says, matter-of-factly. “But it’s not fatal, and it’s not contagious once the initial lust-madness fades. Most of the girls that get it can come back into society after a week or so, though most are kept under medical watch for a while. Once the infection is complete, it’s no longer visible, and the girl’s mind returns to her. It’s hard to get back to normal after you’ve... embarrassed yourself like most victims do, but Command makes allowances for them, finds new jobs for them if needed. Most find themselves well-suited to prostitution, thanks to their libidos, but that’s not always the case.”
rows.translation: “确实，”莉芙平静地说道。“不过它不会致命，最初的情欲癫狂消退后也不再具有传染性。大多数感染者一周左右就能重返社会，不过很多人还会接受一段时间的医疗观察。感染彻底完成后，表面上便再也看不出来，姑娘的理智也会恢复。在你像大多数受害者那样...出尽洋相之后，很难重新回归正常生活，但司令部会照顾她们，必要时还会给她们安排新工作。得益于旺盛的性欲，多数人发现自己很适合从事卖淫，不过也并非人人如此。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“It is,” Lieve says, matter-of-factly. “But it’s not fatal, and it’s not contagious once the initial lust-madness fades. Most of the girls that get it can come back into society after a week or so, though most are kept under medical watch for a while. Once the infection is complete, it’s no longer visible, and the girl’s mind returns to her. It’s hard to get back to normal after you’ve... embarrassed yourself like most victims do, but Command makes allowances for them, finds new jobs for them if needed. Most find themselves well-suited to prostitution, thanks to their libidos, but that’s not always the case.”"

rows.original: You nod your understanding, but you can’t help but add, “You seem to know a lot about this fungus.”
rows.translation: 你点头表示理解，但还是忍不住补充道：“你似乎很了解这种真菌。”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou nod your understanding, but you can’t help but add, “You seem to know a lot about this fungus.”"

rows.original: She shifts again, juggling her weight from one foot to the other. “Of course. We’re all briefed about what to look for, what to avoid. Especially scouts, since our job is to go out alone or in small groups into the caves. We’re especially vulnerable to them because of that, as well as to other monster attacks. The fungus is smart enough not to try and grab a soldier out of a column of fifty or sixty troops, but a lone scout? Well...”
rows.translation: 她再次挪动身子，重心在两只脚之间来回变换。“当然。我们都接受过简报，知道该留意什么、避开什么。尤其是侦察兵，因为我们的工作就是独自或结成小队深入洞穴。正因如此，我们特别容易遭到它们以及其他怪物的袭击。这种真菌很聪明，不会试图从五六十人的队伍里抓走一名士兵，可落单的侦察兵？这个嘛...”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe shifts again, juggling her weight from one foot to the other. “Of course. We’re all briefed about what to look for, what to avoid. Especially scouts, since our job is to go out alone or in small groups into the caves. We’re especially vulnerable to them because of that, as well as to other monster attacks. The fungus is smart enough not to try and grab a soldier out of a column of fifty or sixty troops, but a lone scout? Well...”"

rows.original: “Has one ever tried to infect you?” you ask, curious.
rows.translation: “它们有没有试图感染过你？”你好奇地问。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Has one ever tried to infect you?” you ask, curious."

rows.original: Lieve blanches. “Me? No, no. I carried phosphorous grenades to disperse fungus clouds if they ever got close. Doesn’t kill them, but drives them off in a hurry. It’s a trick we figured out early in the war - they’re not native where we reds come from, just here in goldie territory.”
rows.translation: 莉芙脸色一白。“我？没有，没有。我会携带磷燃手榴弹，在真菌云靠近时驱散它们。杀不死它们，但能让它们赶紧逃开。这是我们在战争初期摸索出的办法——它们并非原产于我们红米尔的家乡，只生长在金米尔的领地。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve blanches. “Me? No, no. I carried phosphorous grenades to disperse fungus clouds if they ever got close. Doesn’t kill them, but drives them off in a hurry. It’s a trick we figured out early in the war - they’re not native where we reds come from, just here in goldie territory.”"

rows.original: You get the distinct feeling Lieve’s not telling you something, but you leave it at that for now.
rows.translation: 你明显感觉莉芙隐瞒了什么，不过暂时没有追问。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou get the distinct feeling Lieve’s not telling you something, but you leave it at that for now."

rows.original: Fungal Myr
rows.translation: 真菌米尔
rows.raw: "Fungal Myr"

rows.original: You ask Lieve if she’d be willing to tell you a little more about the Scarlet Federation’s concept of “citizenship.” From what you’ve heard, it’s very different from being a Confederate citizen, or the citizen of a planet elsewhere in the galaxy, where your citizenship is determined at birth.
rows.translation: 你问莉芙是否愿意多讲讲猩红联邦的“公民身份”观念。根据你听说的情况，这与作为邦联公民或银河系其他星球公民截然不同；在那里，公民身份从出生时便已确定。
rows.raw: "You ask Lieve if she’d be willing to tell you a little more about the Scarlet Federation’s concept of “citizenship.” From what you’ve heard, it’s very different from being a Confederate citizen, or the citizen of a planet elsewhere in the galaxy, where your citizenship is determined at birth."

rows.original: Lieve has a half-smile the entire time you’re talking, drinking up the details of your government and society you divulge with an eager curiosity. When you’re finished, she answers immediately: “No, you’re right. The word means something entirely different for you off-worlders... and for golds... than it does to a red myr. I’m not exactly rated as a Moral Philosophy teacher, but I can try and explain if you’d like. That’s why I’m here, after all.”
rows.translation: 你说话时，莉芙一直面带浅笑，对你透露的政府与社会细节表现出热切的好奇。你讲完后，她立刻答道：“不，你说得对。这个词对你们外星人...还有金米尔...来说，跟对红米尔而言完全不是一回事。我没有道德哲学教师资格，不过你愿意的话，我可以试着解释。毕竟这就是我来这里的原因。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve has a half-smile the entire time you’re talking, drinking up the details of your government and society you divulge with an eager curiosity. When you’re finished, she answers immediately: “No, you’re right. The word means something entirely different for you off-worlders... and for golds... than it does to a red myr. I’m not exactly rated as a Moral Philosophy teacher, but I can try and explain if you’d like. That’s why I’m here, after all.”"

rows.original: Giving her an encouraging nod, you ask Lieve to do her best.
rows.translation: 你鼓励地点点头，请莉芙尽力说明。
rows.raw: "\n\nGiving her an encouraging nod, you ask Lieve to do her best."

rows.original: “I’ll try,” she says with a wink. “Right. The first thing to understand is that nobody is born a citizen of the Federation. Not even the children of the High Commanders. The Scarlet Federation was originally founded by warriors, veterans from our unification wars and the conflict with the nyrea queens around us. The early years were hard, and we survived and stayed together because good people made hard decisions. The Federation doesn’t have the luxury of assured safety and prosperity, and we couldn’t afford to let petty grievances and political machinations get in the way of survival. So the idea of veteran leadership took hold: the idea that the people most qualified to lead us were the people that had fought and bled to bring us together - the people that risked life and limb already for the safety of the Federation.”
rows.translation: “我试试看，”她眨眨眼说道。“好。首先要明白，联邦没有任何人是天生的公民，连最高指挥官的子女也不例外。猩红联邦最初由战士建立，他们是统一战争和对抗周边尼瑞亚女王战争中的老兵。早年生活艰苦，我们能生存下来并团结一致，是因为优秀的人做出了艰难的决定。联邦享受不到有保障的安全与繁荣，也不能让鸡毛蒜皮的怨恨和政治阴谋妨碍生存。于是老兵领导的理念扎下了根：最有资格领导我们的人，就是那些曾为凝聚众人而浴血奋战的人——那些早已为联邦安危冒过生命危险的人。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I’ll try,” she says with a wink. “Right. The first thing to understand is that nobody is born a citizen of the Federation. Not even the children of the High Commanders. The Scarlet Federation was originally founded by warriors, veterans from our unification wars and the conflict with the nyrea queens around us. The early years were hard, and we survived and stayed together because good people made hard decisions. The Federation doesn’t have the luxury of assured safety and prosperity, and we couldn’t afford to let petty grievances and political machinations get in the way of survival. So the idea of veteran leadership took hold: the idea that the people most qualified to lead us were the people that had fought and bled to bring us together - the people that risked life and limb already for the safety of the Federation.”"

rows.original: You nod slowly. <i>“Wouldn’t that
rows.translation: 你缓缓点头。<i>“那不会
rows.raw: "\n\nYou nod slowly. <i>“Wouldn’t that"

rows.original: , like,
rows.translation: ，那个，
rows.raw: ", like,"

rows.original: make your government pretty militaristic?” you ask.
rows.translation: 让你们的政府变得相当军国主义吗？”你问。
rows.raw: " make your government pretty militaristic?” you ask."

rows.original: Lieve smirks. “That’s what the Republic would tell you. But the idea’s the opposite: if you’ve seen combat, you’re going to be the last person in the world to order more girls into the fire unless it’s absolutely necessary. You don’t get to make decisions in the Federation until you’ve proven that you’re willing to lay your life on the line, just like any of the troopers whose lives are in your hands.”
rows.translation: 莉芙得意地笑了。“共和国会这么告诉你。但这个理念恰恰相反：亲历过战斗的人，除非万不得已，否则最不愿再命令姑娘们投身战火。在联邦，只有证明自己愿意像手下任何士兵一样把命押上，才能参与决策。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve smirks. “That’s what the Republic would tell you. But the idea’s the opposite: if you’ve seen combat, you’re going to be the last person in the world to order more girls into the fire unless it’s absolutely necessary. You don’t get to make decisions in the Federation until you’ve proven that you’re willing to lay your life on the line, just like any of the troopers whose lives are in your hands.”"

rows.original: That makes sense, you suppose. Though you have to wonder how the Federation government would work in peace time. Just because you’re a veteran doesn’t mean you’re a capable politician, does it?
rows.translation: 你觉得这有些道理。不过，你不禁怀疑和平时期的联邦政府会如何运作。身为老兵并不意味着善于从政，不是吗？
rows.raw: "\n\nThat makes sense, you suppose. Though you have to wonder how the Federation government would work in peace time. Just because you’re a veteran doesn’t mean you’re a capable politician, does it?"

rows.original: “I hope we’ll find out someday,” Lieve sighs, leaning against the bunker wall. “Even outside of total war, the Federation’s been in some sort of conflict pretty much constantly. Our homeland’s a rough, unforgiving place, and we’ve always been surrounded by enemies. But this war... I hope it will be the last. Through victory, peace.
rows.translation: “希望有一天能知道，”莉芙靠着掩体墙叹息道。“即便不算全面战争，联邦几乎也一直处于某种冲突之中。我们的家园严酷无情，四面向来强敌环伺。但这场战争...我希望它会是最后一场。通过胜利换来和平。
rows.raw: "\n\n“I hope we’ll find out someday,” Lieve sighs, leaning against the bunker wall. “Even outside of total war, the Federation’s been in some sort of conflict pretty much constantly. Our homeland’s a rough, unforgiving place, and we’ve always been surrounded by enemies. But this war... I hope it will be the last. Through victory, peace."

rows.original: Or through diplomacy, if we veterans have anything to say about it.”
rows.translation: 或者通过外交——如果我们这些老兵有发言权的话。”
rows.raw: " Or through diplomacy, if we veterans have anything to say about it.”"

rows.original: “Oh?” you ask. “What do you mean?”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Oh?” you ask. “What do you mean?”"

rows.original: “Between you and me,” Lieve says, giving her captive gold audience a stern look, “rumor has it that High Command is going to issue a referendum on the war soon. With the cease fire looking like it could drag on indefinitely, I think we all just want this to end. If it comes to a vote, the question will be do we re-issue our declaration of war, or do we relent and accept peace? And if we pursue peace, what kind will it be? I think High Command will try and make the Republic a client state, like the nyrean city-states near our territory, but with the star-walkers looming over us... I don’t know. The Republic might squeak out intact in that case, but I’m not sure the Federal government - or its citizens - will settle for that after near total victory. Especially after so much loss to get here.”
rows.translation: “你知我知，”莉芙说着，严厉地看了眼身边被俘的金米尔听众，“有传言说，最高司令部很快会就战争举行全民公投。停火看起来可能无限期拖下去，我想大家只希望这一切结束。真要投票，问题会是：我们重新发布宣战声明，还是退让并接受和平？若追求和平，又会是哪种和平？我想最高司令部会设法让共和国成为附庸国，就像我们领土附近的尼瑞亚城邦一样；但有星行者高悬于我们头顶...我不知道。那样的话，共和国或许能勉强保持完整，可我不确定联邦政府——或其公民——在几乎大获全胜之后是否会接受，尤其是付出了如此惨重的牺牲才走到这里。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Between you and me,” Lieve says, giving her captive gold audience a stern look, “rumor has it that High Command is going to issue a referendum on the war soon. With the cease fire looking like it could drag on indefinitely, I think we all just want this to end. If it comes to a vote, the question will be do we re-issue our declaration of war, or do we relent and accept peace? And if we pursue peace, what kind will it be? I think High Command will try and make the Republic a client state, like the nyrean city-states near our territory, but with the star-walkers looming over us... I don’t know. The Republic might squeak out intact in that case, but I’m not sure the Federal government - or its citizens - will settle for that after near total victory. Especially after so much loss to get here.”"

rows.original: Heavy stuff. You wonder how the vote will go...
rows.translation: 真是沉重。你想知道投票结果会如何...
rows.raw: "\n\nHeavy stuff. You wonder how the vote will go..."

rows.original: Citizenship
rows.translation: 公民身份
rows.raw: "Citizenship"

rows.original: “If you don’t mind my asking, how did you get all those scars?” you ask, slipping around your lover’s side to stroke your hand along her back. She tenses at your question, and even more at your touch.
rows.translation: “如果你不介意我问，你身上那些伤疤是怎么来的？”你绕到爱人身旁，伸手轻抚她的后背。听到你的问题，她身体一僵；被你触碰时，绷得更紧了。
rows.raw: "“If you don’t mind my asking, how did you get all those scars?” you ask, slipping around your lover’s side to stroke your hand along her back. She tenses at your question, and even more at your touch."

rows.original: “Is it rude to ask people... personal questions like that?” Lieve asks, brushing your hands away. “Among your people, I mean.”
rows.translation: “问别人这种...私人问题，算不算失礼？”莉芙拨开你的手，问道。“我是说，在你们那儿。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Is it rude to ask people... personal questions like that?” Lieve asks, brushing your hands away. “Among your people, I mean.”"

rows.original: You muse on that for a moment, letting your hands drop down to Lieve’s waist as you say, “Not among lovers, no...”
rows.translation: 你思索片刻，双手落到莉芙腰间，说道：“恋人之间不算...”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou muse on that for a moment, letting your hands drop down to Lieve’s waist as you say, “Not among lovers, no...”"

rows.original: She grumbles, but doesn’t step away from you again this time. After a few moments her hands find yours, lacing her fingers with yours. “Alright, alright... girls, why don’t you go shopping or something, huh? Here,” she adds, pulling a small coin purse out of her coat and handing it to Mayren. The busty gold girl giggles delightedly and takes Sierva’s hand, leading her companion away and out of the bunker.
rows.translation: 她嘟囔几声，但这次没有再躲开你。片刻后，她找到你的双手，与你十指相扣。“好吧，好吧...姑娘们，你们去逛街什么的，行吗？给，”她补充道，从外套里掏出一个小钱袋递给梅伦。丰满的金米尔姑娘开心地咯咯笑着，牵起希尔瓦的手，带着同伴离开掩体。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe grumbles, but doesn’t step away from you again this time. After a few moments her hands find yours, lacing her fingers with yours. “Alright, alright... girls, why don’t you go shopping or something, huh? Here,” she adds, pulling a small coin purse out of her coat and handing it to Mayren. The busty gold girl giggles delightedly and takes Sierva’s hand, leading her companion away and out of the bunker."

rows.original: When they’re gone, Lieve lets her longcoat slip off her shoulders, then turning back to face you, starts to unbutton her shirt. Slowly, she begins to speak: “You want to know where my scars came from? I’m surprised you had to ask. Not many places a trooper can get cut up like I did.”
rows.translation: 等她们走后，莉芙让长外套从肩头滑落，转身面对你，开始解衬衫纽扣。她缓缓开口：“你想知道我的伤疤从哪儿来？没想到你还需要问。士兵能像我这样被割得遍体鳞伤的地方可不多。”
rows.raw: "\n\nWhen they’re gone, Lieve lets her longcoat slip off her shoulders, then turning back to face you, starts to unbutton her shirt. Slowly, she begins to speak: “You want to know where my scars came from? I’m surprised you had to ask. Not many places a trooper can get cut up like I did.”"

rows.original: Hesitantly, you say that you’re not as experienced with war as Lieve and her people.
rows.translation: 你犹豫地说，自己不像莉芙和她的人民那样熟悉战争。
rows.raw: "Hesitantly, you say that you’re not as experienced with war as Lieve and her people."

rows.original: You nod slowly, but ask her to tell you the story - if she’s up to it.
rows.translation: 你缓缓点头，但请她把故事讲给你听——前提是她愿意。
rows.raw: "You nod slowly, but ask her to tell you the story - if she’s up to it."

rows.original: Lieve seems to think about it for a long moment before pulling her shirt off, revealing the small, pert mounds of her breasts and her flat, tight belly. Your eyes are instantly drawn to the pair of raking scars across her midriff, looking more like a pair of beast’s claws rent her nearly in half than a war wound.
rows.translation: 莉芙似乎考虑了许久，才脱下衬衫，露出小巧挺拔的乳丘和平坦紧实的小腹。你的目光立刻被横贯她腹部的两道爪状伤疤吸引；与其说是战争创伤，更像某头野兽用双爪险些将她撕成两半。
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve seems to think about it for a long moment before pulling her shirt off, revealing the small, pert mounds of her breasts and her flat, tight belly. Your eyes are instantly drawn to the pair of raking scars across her midriff, looking more like a pair of beast’s claws rent her nearly in half than a war wound."

rows.original: She turns around, showing you her back and planting her hands on her hips. Her back is an intricate network of scars, crossing in cruel patterns over each other. Compared to her normally pale, almost albino skin, Lieve’s scars are dark patches of winding vermilion. Her spine presses out against the taut flesh, prominent against her plateless torso. You plant a hand in the small of her back, caressing the rough skin and drawing close to your lover.
rows.translation: 她转过身，向你展示后背，双手叉在腰间。她背上遍布错综复杂的伤疤，残酷地彼此交错。莉芙平常的皮肤苍白得近乎白化，伤疤相比之下则是一片片蜿蜒的朱红。她的脊柱抵着紧绷的皮肤凸显出来，在没有甲片覆盖的躯干上格外醒目。你把手放在她后腰，抚摸粗糙的肌肤，贴近自己的爱人。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe turns around, showing you her back and planting her hands on her hips. Her back is an intricate network of scars, crossing in cruel patterns over each other. Compared to her normally pale, almost albino skin, Lieve’s scars are dark patches of winding vermilion. Her spine presses out against the taut flesh, prominent against her plateless torso. You plant a hand in the small of her back, caressing the rough skin and drawing close to your lover."

rows.original: “You know, for a lot of us red myr, scars are a badge of honor,” Lieve starts, a little more quietly than before. “Go out and ask any of the guards outside to show off their scars, and they’ll be happy to show ‘em off.”
rows.translation: “你知道，对许多红米尔而言，伤疤是荣誉勋章，”莉芙开口说道，声音比先前稍轻。“出去随便请哪个守卫展示伤疤，她们都会很乐意炫耀。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“You know, for a lot of us red myr, scars are a badge of honor,” Lieve starts, a little more quietly than before. “Go out and ask any of the guards outside to show off their scars, and they’ll be happy to show ‘em off.”"

rows.original: “But not you?”
rows.translation: “但你不会？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“But not you?”"

rows.original: Lieve sighs. “Not me. At least, not for those scars. A little over a year ago, I pulled spotter duty. Nothing out of the ordinary - one of the most important things us scouts do is carry radios into No Myr’s Land and spot for artillery. That’s how I met Sierva, even. Dangerous work, and exhausting, but it makes our cannons a hell of a lot more effective. Worth every sweaty, filthy day of curling up in a crater hoping the shells don’t fall just a little bit short and blow me to pieces.”
rows.translation: 莉芙叹了口气。“我不会。至少不会炫耀这些疤。一年多前，我被派去担任炮兵观察员。没什么稀奇——我们侦察兵最重要的任务之一，就是带着无线电深入无米尔之地，为炮兵标定目标。我就是这样认识希尔瓦的。工作危险又累人，却能大幅提升火炮效能。每天汗流浃背、满身污泥地蜷缩在弹坑里，祈祷炮弹别短那么一点把我炸成碎片，也完全值得。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve sighs. “Not me. At least, not for those scars. A little over a year ago, I pulled spotter duty. Nothing out of the ordinary - one of the most important things us scouts do is carry radios into No Myr’s Land and spot for artillery. That’s how I met Sierva, even. Dangerous work, and exhausting, but it makes our cannons a hell of a lot more effective. Worth every sweaty, filthy day of curling up in a crater hoping the shells don’t fall just a little bit short and blow me to pieces.”"

rows.original: “It was the tenth time I’d played spotter, back when the fighting was about fifty miles back east. Everything was going fine until I crawled into a ditch... that happened to have a trap door in it.”
rows.translation: “那是我第十次担任观察员，当时战线还在东边约五十英里处。一切都很顺利，直到我爬进一道沟...而那里面恰好有扇活板门。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“It was the tenth time I’d played spotter, back when the fighting was about fifty miles back east. Everything was going fine until I crawled into a ditch... that happened to have a trap door in it.”"

rows.original: Lieve laughs and shakes her head. “What’re the fucking odds? Of all the craters, ditches, and trenches I could have taken cover in, I’d land right on top of a Republic command bunker. Fell straight through the ceiling and onto their map table. There was about a full second of just stunned silence all around before somebody had the bright idea to rifle butt me.” To illustrate her point, Lieve slaps the heel of her hand into her forehead, right to where you can see a very small, almost unnoticeable scar.
rows.translation: 莉芙笑着摇摇头。“这他妈得多巧？那么多弹坑、沟渠和战壕可以藏身，我偏偏落在共和国的指挥掩体顶上，直接穿过天花板掉到她们的地图桌上。四周足足沉默了一秒，所有人都愣住了，才终于有人灵机一动，用枪托砸我。”为了说明，她用掌根拍向额头，正好落在一道极小、几乎看不出的伤疤上。
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve laughs and shakes her head. “What’re the fucking odds? Of all the craters, ditches, and trenches I could have taken cover in, I’d land right on top of a Republic command bunker. Fell straight through the ceiling and onto their map table. There was about a full second of just stunned silence all around before somebody had the bright idea to rifle butt me.” To illustrate her point, Lieve slaps the heel of her hand into her forehead, right to where you can see a very small, almost unnoticeable scar."

rows.original: “The goldies were already getting desperate by then. We’d pushed them across the ocean, deep into the heartlands. Even their filthy gas couldn’t stop us, they realized. So some of them went a little darker. They wanted - needed - to know how our troops were spread out. Where we’d hidden our artillery batteries and supply depots. How to hit us hardest, in other words. As you might expect, I wasn’t inclined to tell them.”
rows.translation: “那时金米尔已经开始绝望。我们把她们赶过海洋，逼进腹地。她们意识到，就连肮脏的毒气也阻挡不了我们。于是有些人走上了更黑暗的道路。她们想知道——非知道不可——我们的兵力如何部署，炮兵阵地和补给站藏在哪里。换句话说，怎样才能最狠地打击我们。你应该猜得到，我并不想告诉她们。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“The goldies were already getting desperate by then. We’d pushed them across the ocean, deep into the heartlands. Even their filthy gas couldn’t stop us, they realized. So some of them went a little darker. They wanted - needed - to know how our troops were spread out. Where we’d hidden our artillery batteries and supply depots. How to hit us hardest, in other words. As you might expect, I wasn’t inclined to tell them.”"

rows.original: Oh.
rows.translation: 哦。
rows.raw: "\n\nOh."

rows.original: “I ended up in a prisoner camp. Golds don’t believe in trench wives, see - they just shove their P.O.W.s into camps with barely enough food and clothes, maybe some tents or shacks if you’re lucky. They herded us around like hysean slugs, staring down from watch towers full of machine guns and floodlights. It was cold, cramped, and full of sickness. If that wasn’t bad enough, Republic Intelligence would make the rounds every few days. Us officers would get dragged off, one after the other, to answer questions.”
rows.translation: “最后我被关进了战俘营。金米尔不认同战壕妻子这一套——她们只把战俘塞进营地，给勉强够活命的食物和衣服；运气好，或许还有帐篷或棚屋。她们像赶海希恩蛞蝓一样赶着我们，机枪和探照灯林立的瞭望塔居高临下地监视。那里寒冷、拥挤，疾病横行。更糟的是，共和国情报部门每隔几天便会来一轮。我们这些军官一个接一个被拖出去回答问题。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I ended up in a prisoner camp. Golds don’t believe in trench wives, see - they just shove their P.O.W.s into camps with barely enough food and clothes, maybe some tents or shacks if you’re lucky. They herded us around like hysean slugs, staring down from watch towers full of machine guns and floodlights. It was cold, cramped, and full of sickness. If that wasn’t bad enough, Republic Intelligence would make the rounds every few days. Us officers would get dragged off, one after the other, to answer questions.”"

rows.original: Lieve shivers involuntarily, and you find yourself holding her a little closer as a result. “Let’s just say the camp commander was very fond of whips. She had a whole collection she’d parade you through before...”
rows.translation: 莉芙不由自主地颤抖起来，你也因此把她搂得更紧。“就这么说吧，营地指挥官非常喜欢鞭子。她收藏了一整套，每次都会先带你逐一参观，然后再...”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve shivers involuntarily, and you find yourself holding her a little closer as a result. “Let’s just say the camp commander was very fond of whips. She had a whole collection she’d parade you through before...”"

rows.original: You get the picture.
rows.translation: 你已经明白了。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou get the picture."

rows.original: “You asked,” Lieve says, forcing herself to smile as she slips out of your arms.
rows.translation: “是你问的，”莉芙勉强挤出笑容，从你的怀抱中挣开。
rows.raw: "\n\n“You asked,” Lieve says, forcing herself to smile as she slips out of your arms."

rows.original: Her Scars
rows.translation: 她的伤疤
rows.raw: "Her Scars"

rows.original: You have to ask, if the supposedly peace-loving gold myr would resort to something like that, what do the reds do to their prisoners?
rows.translation: 你不得不问：如果据说热爱和平的金米尔都会做出这种事，红米尔又会怎样对待俘虏？
rows.raw: "You have to ask, if the supposedly peace-loving gold myr would resort to something like that, what do the reds do to their prisoners?"

rows.original: Lieve scowls at the implication, but keeps her words more measured than her countenance would suggest. “I can’t speak for everyone, everywhere, Steele. But we don’t do things the way the Republic does. Their government, the damn queens, demonize us. Turn the Federation into a horde of slavering barbarians intent on raping their women and stealing their men. We’re not people to them. It doesn’t matter what they do to us: poison gas, torture, anything they can think up to stave off the inevitable. It’s sick.”
rows.translation: 莉芙因这层暗示皱起眉头，但措辞比表情克制得多。“斯蒂尔，我没法替各地每个人保证。但我们不会像共和国那样做。她们的政府，那些该死的女王，把我们妖魔化成一群垂涎欲滴的野蛮人，只想强奸她们的女人、抢走她们的男人。在她们眼中，我们不是人。所以无论对我们做什么都无所谓：毒气、酷刑，任何能拖延必然结局的手段都行。太恶心了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve scowls at the implication, but keeps her words more measured than her countenance would suggest. “I can’t speak for everyone, everywhere, Steele. But we don’t do things the way the Republic does. Their government, the damn queens, demonize us. Turn the Federation into a horde of slavering barbarians intent on raping their women and stealing their men. We’re not people to them. It doesn’t matter what they do to us: poison gas, torture, anything they can think up to stave off the inevitable. It’s sick.”"

rows.original: A moment passes in silence before her harsh scowl fades into an exhausted sigh. <i>“The gold myr we capture are warriors - worthy of respect, even if they failed. They become our wards, like May and Sierva are to me. If we need to learn something from a prisoner, our venom can get it as surely as a torturer can. It’s not painful. Just the opposite
rows.translation: 沉默片刻后，她严厉的怒容化作疲惫的叹息。<i>“我们俘获的金米尔都是战士——即便战败，也值得尊重。她们会成为我们的受监护人，就像梅和希尔瓦之于我。如果需要从俘虏口中了解什么，我们的毒液和刑讯一样有效，而且并不痛苦，恰恰相反
rows.raw: "\n\nA moment passes in silence before her harsh scowl fades into an exhausted sigh. <i>“The gold myr we capture are warriors - worthy of respect, even if they failed. They become our wards, like May and Sierva are to me. If we need to learn something from a prisoner, our venom can get it as surely as a torturer can. It’s not painful. Just the opposite"

rows.original: , as you well know
rows.translation: ，这一点你很清楚
rows.raw: ", as you well know"

rows.original: . By the time we’re through, they’re begging to tell us anything we want to know in exchange for release. We found out early in the war that venom’s good for more than just fun in the sack.”
rows.translation: 。等我们结束时，她们会求着把我们想知道的一切都说出来，只求得到释放。战争初期我们便发现，毒液除了床上助兴，还有别的用处。”
rows.raw: ". By the time we’re through, they’re begging to tell us anything we want to know in exchange for release. We found out early in the war that venom’s good for more than just fun in the sack.”"

rows.original: You’ve noticed something listening to Lieve, and with her trench wives out for the moment, you don’t mind saying, “The way you talk, you never blame the golds. Only the Republic?”
rows.translation: 听莉芙说话时，你注意到了一件事。她的战壕妻子暂时不在，你便直言道：“照你的说法，你从不责怪金米尔，只责怪共和国？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’ve noticed something listening to Lieve, and with her trench wives out for the moment, you don’t mind saying, “The way you talk, you never blame the golds. Only the Republic?”"

rows.original: Lieve gives you a knowing look as she pulls her shirt back on. “Do you think I’d keep trench wives if I blamed them for everything the Republic’s done? For the war? You can’t blame the soldiers for the decisions of the state, Steele. Every gold myr I’ve ever seen is an unwilling conscript. They hate the war. And if even their own daughters’ hearts aren’t behind them, what does that make the gold queens? Desperate tyrants, the lot of them. If I had my way, when we roll into Gildenmere we’d put the queens against the wall and leave again. Let the golds build something better in their place.”
rows.translation: 莉芙重新穿上衬衫，意味深长地看了你一眼。“如果我把共和国所做的一切、把战争都怪在她们头上，你觉得我还会收战壕妻子吗？斯蒂尔，不能把国家的决定归咎于士兵。我见过的每个金米尔都是被迫征召入伍，她们痛恨战争。连她们自己女儿的心都不站在这一边，那些金米尔女王又算什么？全都是绝望的暴君。如果由我做主，等我们攻入吉尔登米尔，就把女王们推到墙边处决，然后离开。让金米尔在原地建立更好的东西。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve gives you a knowing look as she pulls her shirt back on. “Do you think I’d keep trench wives if I blamed them for everything the Republic’s done? For the war? You can’t blame the soldiers for the decisions of the state, Steele. Every gold myr I’ve ever seen is an unwilling conscript. They hate the war. And if even their own daughters’ hearts aren’t behind them, what does that make the gold queens? Desperate tyrants, the lot of them. If I had my way, when we roll into Gildenmere we’d put the queens against the wall and leave again. Let the golds build something better in their place.”"

rows.original: Harsh.
rows.translation: 真严酷。
rows.raw: "\n\nHarsh."

rows.original: Gold Myr
rows.raw: "Gold Myr"

rows.original: Still, you have to point out, “Don’t the golds need their queens to reproduce? There wouldn’t be much of a race left if you killed all their breeders.”
rows.translation: 不过，你还是得指出：“金米尔不是需要女王来繁衍吗？如果杀光所有育种者，这个种族就剩不了多少了。”
rows.raw: " Still, you have to point out, “Don’t the golds need their queens to reproduce? There wouldn’t be much of a race left if you killed all their breeders.”"

rows.original: Lieve scoffs. <i>“Not every gold breeder can be a queen. Most of them never see a drone in their lives - how would they know?
rows.translation: 莉芙嗤之以鼻。<i>“不是每个金米尔育种者都能成为女王。她们中的大多数一辈子都见不到雄蚁——又怎么知道？
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve scoffs. <i>“Not every gold breeder can be a queen. Most of them never see a drone in their lives - how would they know? "

rows.original: Sierva mentioned she’s never seen a dick before yours. She might very well be a goldie breeder just waiting for her chance.
rows.translation: 希尔瓦说，在你之前她从未见过鸡巴。她很可能就是个只等机会出现的金米尔育种者。
rows.raw: " Sierva mentioned she’s never seen a dick before yours. She might very well be a goldie breeder just waiting for her chance."

rows.original: “And Mayren?”
rows.translation: “那梅伦呢？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“And Mayren?”"

rows.original: “Ha. The day I believe May’s not found a drone to shack up with is the day my plates turn green.”
rows.translation: “哈。等我相信梅从没找雄蚁同居时，我的甲片恐怕都变绿了。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Ha. The day I believe May’s not found a drone to shack up with is the day my plates turn green.”"

rows.original: Must be a local expression, you guess. Lieve continues: <i>“
rows.translation: 你猜这大概是当地说法。莉芙继续道：<i>“
rows.raw: "\n\nMust be a local expression, you guess. Lieve continues: <i>“"

rows.original: Besides, you offworlders are here now. I’ve heard stories about what your medicine can do. Amazing things from the troops that took your fleet’s offer for medical help. A lot of the girls think you might be the cure for our... fertility problems.”
rows.translation: 况且，你们外星人已经来了。我听接受你们舰队医疗援助的士兵讲过，你们的医术能创造奇迹。许多姑娘都觉得，你们或许能解决我们的...生育问题。”
rows.raw: "Besides, you offworlders are here now. I’ve heard stories about what your medicine can do. Amazing things from the troops that took your fleet’s offer for medical help. A lot of the girls think you might be the cure for our... fertility problems.”"

rows.original: You pull Lieve close again, grinning. “I’ll solve your fertility, alright.”
rows.translation: 你再次把莉芙拉近，咧嘴笑道：“好啊，我会解决你的生育需求。”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou pull Lieve close again, grinning. “I’ll solve your fertility, alright.”"

rows.original: <i>“Not YOU, you... you
rows.translation: <i>“不是说你，你这个...你这个
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“Not YOU, you... you "

rows.original: big
rows.translation: 巨大
rows.raw: " big"

rows.original: little
rows.translation: 小小
rows.raw: " little"

rows.original: idiot,” she laughs, planting a kiss on your lips.
rows.translation: 白痴，”她笑着吻上你的嘴唇。
rows.raw: " idiot,” she laughs, planting a kiss on your lips."

rows.original: As she’s finishing, you hear a light knock coming from the bunker’s door. Turning, you see May and Sierva poking their heads in, arms full of shopping bags. “Can we come back yet?” Mayren asks, her eyes as big as a puppy’s.
rows.translation: 她刚说完，你便听见掩体门口传来轻轻的敲门声。转头一看，梅和希尔瓦正探头进来，怀里塞满了购物袋。“我们现在能回来了吗？”梅伦睁着小狗般的大眼睛问。
rows.raw: "\n\nAs she’s finishing, you hear a light knock coming from the bunker’s door. Turning, you see May and Sierva poking their heads in, arms full of shopping bags. “Can we come back yet?” Mayren asks, her eyes as big as a puppy’s."

rows.original: “Yeah. I think we were just finishing up,” Lieve says, waving them in. “Unless Steele has more questions?”
rows.translation: “能。我想我们正好谈完了，”莉芙挥手让她们进来。“除非斯蒂尔还有问题？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Yeah. I think we were just finishing up,” Lieve says, waving them in. “Unless Steele has more questions?”"

rows.original: Red Prisoners?
rows.translation: 红米尔俘虏？
rows.raw: "Red Prisoners?"

rows.original: “You mentioned fertility problems?” you say, looking between the three girls at hand. Despite Lieve’s hardness and Sierva’s slender figure, all of them look like perfect candidates for motherhood by any human standard.
rows.translation: “你刚才提到了生育问题？”你说着，打量眼前的三个姑娘。尽管莉芙身体硬朗，希尔瓦身材纤细，但以人类标准来看，她们全都是完美的母亲人选。
rows.raw: "“You mentioned fertility problems?” you say, looking between the three girls at hand. Despite Lieve’s hardness and Sierva’s slender figure, all of them look like perfect candidates for motherhood by any human standard."

rows.original: “I did,” Lieve answers, eyeing you in a way you can’t quite analyze thanks to her black, solid eyes. “Well, problem might be an exaggeration. Or would be, if there hadn’t been a war. I’m not a statistician, but I know enough about breeding to say both the Federation and the Republic are in trouble, even if the war stays nice and cold for a few generations.”
rows.translation: “是提过，”莉芙回答。她用你无法看透的纯黑双眼打量着你。“不过说是问题，或许有些夸张。如果没有战争，本来也不算问题。我不是统计学家，但对繁育也足够了解，知道即使战争能安稳地冷却几代，联邦与共和国也都处境不妙。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I did,” Lieve answers, eyeing you in a way you can’t quite analyze thanks to her black, solid eyes. “Well, problem might be an exaggeration. Or would be, if there hadn’t been a war. I’m not a statistician, but I know enough about breeding to say both the Federation and the Republic are in trouble, even if the war stays nice and cold for a few generations.”"

rows.original: You cock an eyebrow. “Then what’s the issue?”
rows.translation: 你挑起一边眉毛。“那问题究竟是什么？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou cock an eyebrow. “Then what’s the issue?”"

rows.original: To your surprise, it’s Mayren who speaks up, looking very put out: “We’re infertile! Well, most myr are. Some of us golds can breed a whole bunch and become queens...”
rows.translation: 出乎意料的是，梅伦闷闷不乐地抢先开口：“我们不能生育！嗯，大多数米尔都不能。有些金米尔可以生许多孩子，成为女王...”
rows.raw: "\n\nTo your surprise, it’s Mayren who speaks up, looking very put out: “We’re infertile! Well, most myr are. Some of us golds can breed a whole bunch and become queens...”"

rows.original: “And a little less than half of us reds can lay a few eggs,” Lieve finishes. “Plus only one in ten myr are men, on either side. Both the Federation and the Republic have lost more breeders than we’ve gained in the fighting. Even if we don’t glass ourselves, and you offworlders don’t decide to step on us all from on high, we might just die out anyway. Hell of a sendoff that’ll be.”
rows.translation: “我们红米尔中，能产下几枚卵的也不到一半，”莉芙接着说。“而且无论哪一方，雄性都只有十分之一。联邦和共和国在战斗中损失的育种者都超过了新增数量。即便我们没有把自己烧成玻璃，你们外星人也没决定从天而降把我们全部踩死，我们或许还是会自行灭绝。这可真是够体面的谢幕。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“And a little less than half of us reds can lay a few eggs,” Lieve finishes. “Plus only one in ten myr are men, on either side. Both the Federation and the Republic have lost more breeders than we’ve gained in the fighting. Even if we don’t glass ourselves, and you offworlders don’t decide to step on us all from on high, we might just die out anyway. Hell of a sendoff that’ll be.”"

rows.original: You grimace at Lieve’s sudden grimness. “And how are we offworlders supposed to help, exactly?”
rows.translation: 莉芙突然如此悲观，令你面露苦色。“那我们外星人究竟该怎么帮？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou grimace at Lieve’s sudden grimness. “And how are we offworlders supposed to help, exactly?”"

rows.original: In answer, Lieve jabs a finger at your Codex. “I’ve seen a few aliens with devices like that. Computers. You know, we’ve got computers too. They’re the size of warehouses, and take hours to do anything. You’ve got weapons that could crack our planet in half and send us all gasping into space. Airplanes that can travel between worlds where ours can’t make it across the ocean without a carrier.”
rows.translation: 作为回答，莉芙伸手指向你的宝典。“我见过几个外星人拿着类似的设备。电脑。你知道，我们也有电脑，但有仓库那么大，做什么都要花上几个小时。你们有能把我们的星球劈成两半、让所有人窒息着飞进太空的武器；还有能在世界之间航行的飞机，而我们的飞机没有航空母舰甚至飞不过海洋。”
rows.raw: "\n\nIn answer, Lieve jabs a finger at your Codex. “I’ve seen a few aliens with devices like that. Computers. You know, we’ve got computers too. They’re the size of warehouses, and take hours to do anything. You’ve got weapons that could crack our planet in half and send us all gasping into space. Airplanes that can travel between worlds where ours can’t make it across the ocean without a carrier.”"

rows.original: You guess she means starships, but hey.
rows.translation: 你猜她指的是星舰，不过算了。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou guess she means starships, but hey."

rows.original: “And your medicine? When the... ow-soor... right?”
rows.translation: “还有你们的医术？当那些...奥——索尔...对吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“And your medicine? When the... ow-soor... right?”"

rows.original: “Ausar,” you correct when you realize it’s not a translator error, but Lieve actually trying to pronounce the word.
rows.translation: “奥萨尔，”你纠正道，因为你意识到这并非翻译器出错，而是莉芙真的在尝试发出这个词。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Ausar,” you correct when you realize it’s not a translator error, but Lieve actually trying to pronounce the word."

rows.original: “When the ausar fleet showed up in orbit, their medics offered to help a lot of our wounded. The troops we sent up came back with robotic parts in place of missing limbs, wounds healed that our best doctors would have called fatal. A few shipments of medicine has almost completely wiped out the thraadi flu. You can even change your bodies, swapping parts around like it’s nothing!”
rows.translation: “当奥萨尔舰队出现在轨道上时，他们的医护人员主动救治了我们许多伤员。我们送上去的士兵回来时，缺失的肢体被机械部件替代；我们最好的医生认为致命的伤势也痊愈了。几批药物几乎彻底消灭了思拉迪流感。你们甚至能改变身体，像没什么大不了的一样随意替换部位！”
rows.raw: "\n\n“When the ausar fleet showed up in orbit, their medics offered to help a lot of our wounded. The troops we sent up came back with robotic parts in place of missing limbs, wounds healed that our best doctors would have called fatal. A few shipments of medicine has almost completely wiped out the thraadi flu. You can even change your bodies, swapping parts around like it’s nothing!”"

rows.original: It’s hardly nothing, but you get her point. “You think we can make you all fertile?”
rows.translation: 这绝非没什么大不了，但你理解她的意思。“你觉得我们能让你们全都恢复生育能力？”
rows.raw: "\n\nIt’s hardly nothing, but you get her point. “You think we can make you all fertile?”"

rows.original: “You could do a lot more than that. Imagine if every girl had a male if she wanted one, if every woman could bear children. We could do more than rebuild, we could flourish! What if this war was nothing more than a bump in the road, not us teetering on the edge of extinction? My people, the Federation, would do anything for that. I swear, if whatever government is out there for you aliens would do that for us, you’d have the staunchest allies you could ever imagine.”
rows.translation: “你们能做的远不止这些。想象一下，每个姑娘想要时都能拥有一个男人，每个女人都能生育。我们不仅可以重建，还能繁荣！如果这场战争不过是路上的一道坎，而不是让我们在灭绝边缘摇摇欲坠呢？我的人民、联邦愿意为此付出任何代价。我发誓，如果你们外星人的政府愿意为我们做到这一点，就会得到最坚定的盟友。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“You could do a lot more than that. Imagine if every girl had a male if she wanted one, if every woman could bear children. We could do more than rebuild, we could flourish! What if this war was nothing more than a bump in the road, not us teetering on the edge of extinction? My people, the Federation, would do anything for that. I swear, if whatever government is out there for you aliens would do that for us, you’d have the staunchest allies you could ever imagine.”"

rows.original: You don’t think you’ve ever seen Lieve this impassioned, even when making love. You go to put a reassuring hand on her shoulder, but she intercepts it, grabbing your hand in hers. “Work with us, Steele. Give us a generation to recover. Your diplomats say they want that, right? Cooperation? If they’d cooperate with the Federation, we could be right out there beside you in the galaxy. Your shield and your hammer, if you’d have us.”
rows.translation: 你从未见过莉芙如此激昂，就连做爱时也没有。你伸手想安慰地按住她的肩，却被她半途截住，握进手中。“与我们合作吧，斯蒂尔。给我们一代人的时间恢复。你们的外交官说他们想要这个，对吧？合作？如果他们愿意与联邦合作，我们就能在银河中与你们并肩。只要你们愿意接纳，我们会成为你们的盾与锤。”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou don’t think you’ve ever seen Lieve this impassioned, even when making love. You go to put a reassuring hand on her shoulder, but she intercepts it, grabbing your hand in hers. “Work with us, Steele. Give us a generation to recover. Your diplomats say they want that, right? Cooperation? If they’d cooperate with the Federation, we could be right out there beside you in the galaxy. Your shield and your hammer, if you’d have us.”"

rows.original: You can’t imagine the Confederacy uplifting a race just to be soldiers, but the offer is so passionate that you can’t help but appreciate the offer.
rows.translation: 你无法想象邦联会仅仅为了培养士兵而提升一个种族，但这番提议如此热情，你仍不禁心怀感激。
rows.raw: "You can’t imagine the Confederacy uplifting a race just to be soldiers, but the offer is so passionate that you can’t help but appreciate the offer."

rows.original: It’s hard to refuse an offer like that! You could certainly picture a few uses for your own army of ant amazons. Maybe you ought to talk to Steele Tech about some... relief efforts? Corporate could probably write it off on their taxes.
rows.translation: 如此提议实在难以拒绝！你当然能想到几种运用私人蚁族亚马逊军团的方式。也许该和斯蒂尔科技谈谈某些...救济行动？公司大概还能拿去抵税。
rows.raw: "It’s hard to refuse an offer like that! You could certainly picture a few uses for your own army of ant amazons. Maybe you ought to talk to Steele Tech about some... relief efforts? Corporate could probably write it off on their taxes."

rows.original: Now that’s an offer that’s hard to refuse. Whoever helps the red myr first would be a force to be reckoned with in a generation.
rows.translation: 这才真是难以拒绝的提议。无论谁率先帮助红米尔，一代之后都会成为一股不容小觑的力量。
rows.raw: "Now that’s an offer that’s hard to refuse. Whoever helps the red myr first would be a force to be reckoned with in a generation."

rows.original: Smiling, you turn to your insectile lover and tell her, “Maybe you should have been the Federation ambassador.”
rows.translation: 你微笑着转向自己的虫族爱人，告诉她：“也许联邦大使本该由你来当。”
rows.raw: " Smiling, you turn to your insectile lover and tell her, “Maybe you should have been the Federation ambassador.”"

rows.original: Lieve laughs at that. Good, honest, humor written across her features. “I’m sure Colonel Nehzara would be thrilled to trade places with me, too, even if they bumped her back down to buck private.”
rows.translation: 莉芙笑了起来，脸上洋溢着真挚而坦率的喜悦。“我相信内扎拉上校也会很乐意跟我换位置，哪怕他们把她一路降回列兵。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve laughs at that. Good, honest, humor written across her features. “I’m sure Colonel Nehzara would be thrilled to trade places with me, too, even if they bumped her back down to buck private.”"

rows.original: Sharing her smile, you ask if she’d take the post, given the chance. That makes her think for a second. “I think I would, yes. If it would help my people, I’d take Nehzara’s spot in a heartbeat. Not that anybody’s offering me, though. I’m just a poor farm girl who barely made it to officer. High Command doesn’t even know I exist.”
rows.translation: 你也笑着问她，如果有机会是否愿意接受这个职位。她想了一会儿。“我想我会的，没错。如果能帮助人民，我会毫不犹豫地接替内扎拉。不过也没人会邀请我。我只是个勉强升上军官的穷苦农家姑娘，最高司令部甚至不知道我的存在。”
rows.raw: "\n\nSharing her smile, you ask if she’d take the post, given the chance. That makes her think for a second. “I think I would, yes. If it would help my people, I’d take Nehzara’s spot in a heartbeat. Not that anybody’s offering me, though. I’m just a poor farm girl who barely made it to officer. High Command doesn’t even know I exist.”"

rows.original: “And where do the gold myr fit into this future of yours, exactly?” Sierva asks, looking up to her mistress with a playful glint in her eye.
rows.translation: “那我们金米尔在你的未来里究竟处于什么位置？”希尔瓦问道，眼中带着调皮的光芒，仰望自己的女主人。
rows.raw: "\n\n“And where do the gold myr fit into this future of yours, exactly?” Sierva asks, looking up to her mistress with a playful glint in her eye."

rows.original: Lieve answers by grabbing the gold warrior’s ass, making her gasp pleasurably. “Heh, if we get to go out to the stars, fuck it, you can have this dry dirtball of a planet. But honestly... if we ever could hammer out a peace treaty, I don’t see why you couldn’t come along for the ride. I’m sure our alien friends would love all your art and music and... whatever.”
rows.translation: 莉芙一把抓住这位金色战士的屁股，令她愉悦地倒抽一口气。“嘿，要是我们真能飞向群星，那管他的，这颗干巴巴的泥球就留给你们。但老实说...如果我们真能谈成和平条约，我看不出你们为什么不能一同上路。我相信我们的外星朋友会喜欢你们所有的艺术、音乐和...随便什么。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve answers by grabbing the gold warrior’s ass, making her gasp pleasurably. “Heh, if we get to go out to the stars, fuck it, you can have this dry dirtball of a planet. But honestly... if we ever could hammer out a peace treaty, I don’t see why you couldn’t come along for the ride. I’m sure our alien friends would love all your art and music and... whatever.”"

rows.original: May and Sierva giggle at that, and let the topic slide.
rows.translation: 梅和希尔瓦闻言咯咯发笑，就此放过了这个话题。
rows.raw: "\n\nMay and Sierva giggle at that, and let the topic slide."

rows.original: Myr Fertility
rows.translation: 米尔生育能力
rows.raw: "Myr Fertility"

rows.original: Neoptolemus
rows.raw: "Neoptolemus"

rows.original: “I’m looking for an offworld probe that crash landed somewhere around here.” You explain to her. “Have you or any of the other scouts seen anything like that out in the tunnels?”
rows.translation: “我在寻找一枚坠毁在这附近某处的外星探针。”你向她解释。“你或其他侦察兵在隧道中见过类似的东西吗？”
rows.raw: "“I’m looking for an offworld probe that crash landed somewhere around here.” You explain to her. “Have you or any of the other scouts seen anything like that out in the tunnels?”"

rows.original: Lieve considers this for a moment. “My unit certainly hasn’t recovered any offworld artifacts, but there was something...” she trails off and turns around to rifle through a bag lying against the bunker wall. A moment later Lieve straightens back up and unfolds a battered map. You can’t make out most of it, but from the general area and the mass of scribbled annotations, you guess that the Myr scouts use it to record their discoveries in the caverns. “There we go, just before the ceasefire there was some sort of explosion west of here.”
rows.translation: 莉芙思索片刻。“我的部队肯定没有回收过任何外星遗物，但确实有件事...”她拖长话音，转身翻找靠在掩体墙边的袋子。片刻后，莉芙重新站直，展开一张破旧地图。大部分内容你看不懂，但从大致区域和密密麻麻的潦草批注来看，你猜米尔侦察兵会用它记录洞穴中的发现。“找到了，就在停火前，这里以西发生过某种爆炸。”
rows.raw: "\n\nLieve considers this for a moment. “My unit certainly hasn’t recovered any offworld artifacts, but there was something...” she trails off and turns around to rifle through a bag lying against the bunker wall. A moment later Lieve straightens back up and unfolds a battered map. You can’t make out most of it, but from the general area and the mass of scribbled annotations, you guess that the Myr scouts use it to record their discoveries in the caverns. “There we go, just before the ceasefire there was some sort of explosion west of here.”"

rows.original: “Command was worried the Golds had come up with some kind of new secret weapon.” She grimaces. “Sounds stupid now, but after the poison gas, we were all nervous about that. Anyway, we did some reconnaissance there. Something had punched down through a couple of layers of caverns, but other than that there wasn’t much to see.”
rows.translation: “司令部担心金米尔研制出了某种新型秘密武器。”她扮了个苦相。“现在听起来很蠢，但经历毒气后，我们都对此提心吊胆。总之，我们去那里侦察过。有什么东西击穿了好几层洞穴，不过除此之外没什么可看的。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Command was worried the Golds had come up with some kind of new secret weapon.” She grimaces. “Sounds stupid now, but after the poison gas, we were all nervous about that. Anyway, we did some reconnaissance there. Something had punched down through a couple of layers of caverns, but other than that there wasn’t much to see.”"

rows.original: You nod encouragingly, this could be what you’re looking for. Those probes certainly looked like they were designed to take a heavy beating.
rows.translation: 你鼓励地点点头，这或许正是你要找的东西。那些探针看起来的确经得起猛烈撞击。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou nod encouragingly, this could be what you’re looking for. Those probes certainly looked like they were designed to take a heavy beating."

rows.original: “If you really want to check it out for yourself, head south west of here, you’ll find a ledge you can rappel down to reach the deep caverns. But you want to be prepared. Bad as it out there,” Lieve points towards the unoccupied tunnels that stretch away outside the pillbox. “It’s even worse in the deep caverns.”
rows.translation: “如果你真想亲自去看看，就从这里向西南走。你会找到一道可以垂降到深层洞穴的岩架。不过你得做好准备。外面已经够糟了，”莉芙指向碉堡外延伸而去、无人驻守的隧道。“深层洞穴里更糟。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“If you really want to check it out for yourself, head south west of here, you’ll find a ledge you can rappel down to reach the deep caverns. But you want to be prepared. Bad as it out there,” Lieve points towards the unoccupied tunnels that stretch away outside the pillbox. “It’s even worse in the deep caverns.”"

rows.original: Probe
rows.translation: 探针
rows.raw: "Probe"

rows.original: Probe
rows.translation: 探针
rows.raw: "Probe"

rows.original: Steele Tech Probe
rows.translation: 斯蒂尔科技探针
rows.raw: "Steele Tech Probe"

rows.original: Lieve’s a scout, right? Maybe she knows something about where your dad’s probe ended up.
rows.translation: 莉芙是侦察兵，对吧？也许她知道你父亲的探针落到了哪里。
rows.raw: "Lieve’s a scout, right? Maybe she knows something about where your dad’s probe ended up."

rows.original: Back
rows.translation: 返回
rows.raw: "Back"

rows.original: Talk
rows.translation: 交谈
rows.raw: "Talk"

rows.original: Lieve’s offering, so ask her a few questions.
rows.translation: 既然莉芙主动提出了，那就问她几个问题。
rows.raw: "Lieve’s offering, so ask her a few questions."

rows.original: Sex
rows.translation: 做爱

rows.original: Sierva’s smile fades completely, replaced by a hurt look as she answers, “I was wounded in action. Our battalion was supposed to take back a town from the Federation, a surface access town called Ferenze. The enemy was entrenched, though, and we walked into a solid wall of machinegun fire. I called a retreat when I realized the attack was hopeless, but took a round in the hip on the way back to our line. Ended up falling into a shell crater, left behind and bleeding out. I laid there for hours... the pain was incredible. Even if my troops realized they’d left me behind, there was nothing they could do to help with all those Federation guns aimed at them.”

Dragged me back to a Federation aid station and ordered their medics to patch me up. Another hour, they said later, and I’d have bled out completely.”
